content:
Update the existing Krisiveda "Disease & Medicine" section so that the real disease images already stored inside the project's public folder are used consistently throughout the UI.

IMPORTANT:
Do NOT generate new images.
Do NOT create illustrations.
Do NOT replace the existing images with AI-generated graphics.
Use the exact image files already present in the public/Disease folder.

CURRENT STRUCTURE:
- Disease & Medicine has disease cards.
- Each card currently has a small disease image/logo.
- Clicking a card opens the floating Disease Details window/modal.
- The floating window currently uses a generic/illustrated disease graphic at the top.

GOAL:
Use the REAL disease photographs from public/Disease for BOTH:
1. The small image/logo displayed on each disease card.
2. The large image displayed inside the floating Disease Details window.

The image used in the floating window must correspond exactly to the disease that was clicked.

IMAGE FILES AVAILABLE IN public/Disease:

- Bacterial Leaf Blight (BLB).jpg
- bacterial leaf streak.jpg
- Bakanae_Foot Rot.jpg
- brown plant hopper.jpg
- Brown Spot.jpg
- False Smut.jpg
- iron toxicity.jpg
- Khaira Disease.jpg
- Leaf Blast.jpg
- Rice Tungro.jpg
- Rice Yellow Dwarf.jpg
- Root-Knot.jpg
- Sheath Blight.jpg
- Ufra Disease.jpg

Use these exact files and their actual filenames.

DISEASE → IMAGE MAPPING:

Bacterial Leaf Blight (BLB)
→ public/Disease/Bacterial Leaf Blight (BLB).jpg

Bacterial Leaf Streak
→ public/Disease/bacterial leaf streak.jpg

Bakanae / Foot Rot
→ public/Disease/Bakanae_Foot Rot.jpg

Brown Plant Hopper
→ public/Disease/brown plant hopper.jpg

Brown Spot
→ public/Disease/Brown Spot.jpg

False Smut
→ public/Disease/False Smut.jpg

Iron Toxicity
→ public/Disease/iron toxicity.jpg

Khaira Disease
→ public/Disease/Khaira Disease.jpg

Leaf Blast
→ public/Disease/Leaf Blast.jpg

Rice Tungro Disease
→ public/Disease/Rice Tungro.jpg

Rice Yellow Dwarf
→ public/Disease/Rice Yellow Dwarf.jpg

Root-Knot
→ public/Disease/Root-Knot.jpg

Sheath Blight
→ public/Disease/Sheath Blight.jpg

Ufra Disease
→ public/Disease/Ufra Disease.jpg


CARD IMAGES:
- Replace the existing disease card thumbnail/logo with the corresponding real photograph.
- Keep the existing card layout, card dimensions, typography, severity badge, treatment information, cost, symptoms and "View Details" button.
- Only replace the image source.
- Keep the image in a clean contained thumbnail area.
- Use object-fit: cover where appropriate.
- Do not distort the original image.
- Do not crop important disease details unnecessarily.

FLOATING DETAILS WINDOW:
When a disease card is clicked:
- Replace the current illustrated/vector disease graphic at the top of the floating details window with the corresponding real photograph from public/Disease.
- The image must match the selected disease exactly.
- Example:
  Clicking "Leaf Blast" → show Leaf Blast.jpg.
  Clicking "Brown Spot" → show Brown Spot.jpg.
  Clicking "Sheath Blight" → show Sheath Blight.jpg.
  Clicking "Bacterial Leaf Blight (BLB)" → show Bacterial Leaf Blight (BLB).jpg.
- Do not use one generic image for all diseases.
- Do not generate or recreate the disease image.

FLOATING WINDOW IMAGE DESIGN:
Keep the existing floating modal/window design, glass/dark styling, close button, disease title, scientific name, severity badge, recommended treatment, dose, coverage, treatment cost, symptoms, commonly seen in, and Ask AI section.

Only replace the large top illustration/image.

For the new photograph:
- Place it inside the same existing image area.
- Keep the same overall modal dimensions.
- Use a clean rounded container.
- Use object-fit: cover or contain based on the original aspect ratio so the photograph looks natural.
- Do not stretch the image.
- Do not apply heavy filters.
- Do not overlay fake disease markings.
- Keep the original photograph visually clear.

DATA ARCHITECTURE:
Do not hardcode separate image URLs independently inside every card and modal.

Create/use a single disease data structure where each disease has an image property, for example conceptually:

disease.image = "/Disease/Leaf Blast.jpg"

Then use that same image property for:
- Disease card thumbnail
- Floating details modal image

This ensures the card and modal can never become mismatched.

IMPORTANT VITE/GITHUB PAGES:
This project is deployed using Vite/GitHub Pages.

Use the existing project's base-path-safe asset handling.

Do NOT assume the root path will always be "/".
If the project already uses import.meta.env.BASE_URL or another existing asset helper, follow that existing approach.

Make sure filenames containing:
- spaces
- parentheses
- underscores
- hyphens

are handled correctly.

Do not rename the existing image files unless absolutely necessary.

RESPONSIVE BEHAVIOR:
- Desktop: preserve the existing card grid and modal layout.
- Mobile: preserve the existing mobile card layout and floating modal behavior.
- The new real images must scale correctly on both desktop and mobile.
- Do not increase the modal height unnecessarily.
- Do not cause horizontal overflow.

IMPORTANT:
Do not change any disease information, treatment text, medicine names, dosage, cost, symptoms, severity, or other existing content.

Do not redesign the Disease & Medicine page.

Do not change:
- Sidebar
- Search
- Filter chips
- Disease cards layout
- Modal structure
- Modal animation
- Close button
- Ask AI section
- Navigation
- Theme
- Responsive behavior

ONLY change the disease image system so that the real photographs from public/Disease are used consistently in the cards and their corresponding floating details windows.

Before finishing, verify every available image filename in public/Disease and make sure each disease card and its modal use the correct matching photograph.

import { createClient } from "@supabase/supabase-js";

const supabaseUrl = import.meta.env.VITE_SUPABASE_URL;
const supabaseAnonKey = import.meta.env.VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY;

        "  VITE_SUPABASE_URL=https://quietlempkeldflcutpg.supabase.co\n" +

        "Then restart the dev server.",
    );
}

{"kind":"tool","id":"zwHevmgZRlM","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"src/components/auth/ProtectedRoute.jsx","instructions":"Create ProtectedRoute: shows a minimal splash while the session initializes, redirects unauthenticated users to /login preserving the attempted location.","content":"/**
 * ProtectedRoute.jsx — gate for authenticated-only areas.
 *
 * • While the initial session check runs (refreshing the page), a minimal
 *   splash renders instead of flashing the login screen.
 * • Unauthenticated visitors are redirected to /login; the attempted
 *   location is remembered so login can return them to it.
 * • Already-authenticated visitors hitting /login or /signup bounce back
 *   to the app (handled inside Login/Signup via the same pattern).
 *
 * Pure routing logic — zero styling coupling; the splash markup is the
 * only presentational bit and is trivially replaceable.
 */

import { Navigate, useLocation } from "react-router-dom";
import { useAuth } from "../../hooks/useAuth";

export default function ProtectedRoute({ children }) {
    const { isAuthenticated, initializing } = useAuth();
    const location = useLocation();

    if (initializing) {
        // Session restore in flight (e.g. page refresh) — hold the shell.
        return (
            <div style={{ minHeight: "100vh", display: "grid", placeItems: "center" }}>
                <span aria-live="polite">Loading…</span>
            </div>
        );
    }

    if (!isAuthenticated) {
        // Remember where the user wanted to go; Login sends them back here.
        return <Navigate to="/login" replace state={{ from: location.pathname }} />;
    }

    return children;
}

{"kind":"tool","id":"zwLc30OnTYI","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"src/components/auth/authValidation.js","instructions":"Create pure client-side validation helpers for login and signup forms, returning field-level error strings.","content":"/**
 * authValidation.js — pure client-side form validation (no React).
 *
 * Returns field-level error strings for the Login/Signup UIs. Kept as a
 * separate tiny module so the rules are testable and the UI stays dumb.
 */

const EMAIL_RE = /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/;

export function validateEmail(email) {
    if (!email || !email.trim()) return "Email is required.";
    if (!EMAIL_RE.test(email.trim())) return "Please enter a valid email address.";
    return "";
}

export function validatePassword(password) {
    if (!password) return "Password is required.";
    if (password.length < 6) return "Password must be at least 6 characters.";
    return "";
}

export function validateConfirmPassword(password, confirm) {
    if (!confirm) return "Please confirm your password.";
    if (password !== confirm) return "Passwords do not match.";
    return "";
}

/** Full login check → { email, password } error map (empty strings = ok). */
export function validateLogin({ email, password }) {
    return {
        email: validateEmail(email),
        password: validatePassword(password),
    };
}

/** Full signup check → { email, password, confirm } error map. */
export function validateSignup({ email, password, confirm }) {
    return {
        email: validateEmail(email),
        password: validatePassword(password),
        confirm: validateConfirmPassword(password, confirm),
    };
}

export const hasErrors = (map) => Object.values(map).some(Boolean);

+/**
+ * supabaseClient.js — THE single Supabase client for the whole app.
+ *
+ * One client, one import site. Never create another client elsewhere —
+ * Supabase keeps its session/observer state inside the client instance,
+ * so a second client would silently fork the auth state.
+ *
+ * Credentials come from Vite env vars (.env — never committed):
+ *   VITE_SUPABASE_URL        e.g. https://quietlempkeldflcutpg.supabase.co
+ *   VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY   the Publishable/anon key (safe for browsers)
+ *
+ * Only the PUBLIC anon/publishable key ever lives in frontend code.
+ * The service_role / secret keys must NEVER appear here.
+ */
+
+import { createClient } from "@supabase/supabase-js";
+
+const supabaseUrl = import.meta.env.VITE_SUPABASE_URL;
+const supabaseAnonKey = import.meta.env.VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY;
+
+/** Fail loudly (and only in dev) when env vars are missing, instead of
+ *  letting the app boot with a broken client that fails at first auth
+ *  call with a confusing error. */
+if (!supabaseUrl || !supabaseAnonKey || supabaseAnonKey === "YOUR_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY") {
+    // eslint-disable-next-line no-console

+        "  VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=<your Supabase Publishable key>\n" +
+        "Then restart the dev server.",
+    );
+}
+

Perform a COMPLETE performance optimization pass on the existing Krisiveda website to make the entire website feel ULTRA-SMOOTH, fast, responsive, and premium during scrolling, navigation, opening/closing UI elements, and general interaction.

IMPORTANT:
This is a PERFORMANCE optimization task.

DO NOT redesign the website.
DO NOT remove existing features.
DO NOT change the existing visual design unnecessarily.
DO NOT add scroll animations.
Currently there are NO scroll-triggered animations, and I want to keep it that way.

The goal is to make the existing website feel as smooth as a highly optimized modern production website.

==================================================
1. FIRST — AUDIT THE ENTIRE PROJECT
==================================================

Before changing code, inspect the existing project and identify the actual causes of lag.

Check:

- React component re-renders
- unnecessary state updates
- unnecessary effects
- expensive useEffect dependencies
- repeated calculations during render
- large lists
- image loading
- image decoding
- CSS repaint-heavy properties
- backdrop-filter usage
- filter usage
- box-shadow usage
- animated gradients
- animated borders
- event listeners
- resize listeners
- scroll listeners
- timers
- intervals
- requestAnimationFrame usage
- unnecessary DOM nesting
- large DOM trees
- components that render even when not visible
- modal rendering
- weather updates
- location/weather API updates
- voice mode state updates
- profile state updates
- notification state updates

Do not blindly optimize random files.

Find the real bottlenecks first.

==================================================
2. ZERO SCROLL-BASED RE-RENDERS
==================================================

Since the website currently has NO scroll animation, keep scrolling completely independent from React state.

Do NOT create:

scroll → setState → render

Do NOT use React state for scroll position unless absolutely required.

If any existing scroll listener updates React state unnecessarily, remove/optimize it.

If a scroll listener is actually required:
- use passive listeners
- throttle appropriately
- prefer requestAnimationFrame when visual updates are genuinely required
- never trigger unnecessary component-wide re-renders

Scrolling should be handled primarily by the browser's native compositor.

==================================================
3. MAKE SCROLLING ULTRA SMOOTH
==================================================

Optimize the page so normal scrolling feels:

- smooth
- stable
- responsive
- low-latency
- no micro-stutters
- no sudden frame drops

Do NOT add fake smooth-scroll libraries just to make scrolling appear smoother.

Prefer native browser scrolling.

Do NOT use JavaScript-driven scrolling for normal page scrolling.

Avoid unnecessary:

scroll-behavior: smooth

on the entire application if it causes performance issues.

Use native scrolling unless there is a specific reason otherwise.

==================================================
4. REDUCE EXPENSIVE PAINT OPERATIONS
==================================================

Inspect all existing CSS for expensive visual effects.

Pay particular attention to:

- backdrop-filter
- filter
- large blur values
- large box-shadow
- animated box-shadow
- animated filter
- animated background
- animated gradients
- large radial gradients
- multiple overlapping gradients
- large translucent layers

DO NOT remove these effects blindly.

Preserve the current visual appearance where possible.

Instead, optimize them.

For example:
- keep blur localized to small surfaces
- avoid huge full-screen blur layers
- avoid repeatedly repainting large areas
- avoid animating expensive CSS properties
- use pseudo-elements for decorative effects where appropriate
- isolate expensive visual layers when beneficial

==================================================
5. GPU-FRIENDLY ANIMATIONS
==================================================

For existing animations, prefer:

transform
opacity

These should be the primary animated properties.

Avoid animating:

width
height
top
left
margin
padding
border-width
box-shadow
filter
background-position
background-size

unless absolutely necessary.

Do NOT redesign existing animations.

Only change their implementation when necessary to improve performance while keeping the same visual result.

==================================================
6. OPTIMIZE EXISTING AURORA / GRADIENT EFFECTS
==================================================

The website contains several animated gradient/border effects.

Keep them visually intact.

However:

- avoid animating huge background surfaces
- avoid unnecessary repainting of entire cards
- isolate decorative animation layers
- use pseudo-elements where appropriate
- animate transform instead of expensive properties when possible
- keep animated layers small
- avoid multiple independent animations when one composited layer can achieve the same effect

IMPORTANT:

Do NOT make the gradients weaker just for performance.

Keep the current visual quality.

==================================================
7. OPTIMIZE GLASS / BLUR EFFECTS
==================================================

The website uses translucent/glass UI.

Keep the glass aesthetic.

But optimize:

backdrop-filter: blur(...)

especially when used on:
- large containers
- full-screen overlays
- multiple nested elements
- multiple cards visible simultaneously

Avoid nested backdrop blurs.

If multiple layers are blurring the same area, consolidate them where possible.

The final appearance should remain visually similar while requiring less rendering work.

==================================================
8. IMAGE PERFORMANCE
==================================================

Audit ALL images used by Krisiveda.

Especially:

- Crop/Disease images
- Rice variety images
- Profile images
- Weather assets
- other large images

Implement:

- lazy loading for below-the-fold images
- proper width/height or aspect-ratio to prevent layout shifts
- responsive image sizing where appropriate
- avoid loading huge source images when a smaller display size is sufficient
- decode images efficiently
- avoid repeatedly decoding the same image

Do NOT break existing image paths.

Do NOT change the actual visual content.

For images that are immediately visible above the fold, avoid lazy-loading if it would delay their appearance.

==================================================
9. PREVENT LAYOUT SHIFT
==================================================

Make sure images, cards, weather content, and dynamic components reserve their space before content loads.

Use:

- aspect-ratio
- width/height
- fixed/minimum dimensions where appropriate

Avoid elements suddenly jumping when:

- weather loads
- profile image loads
- disease image loads
- market data loads
- location loads

The page should remain visually stable.

==================================================
10. REACT RENDER OPTIMIZATION
==================================================

Inspect components for unnecessary re-renders.

Use appropriate techniques such as:

- React.memo
- useMemo
- useCallback

ONLY where they actually provide benefit.

Do NOT wrap every component in React.memo.

Do NOT add useMemo/useCallback everywhere blindly.

Focus on components that:
- receive stable props
- are expensive to render
- update frequently
- contain large DOM trees
- contain lists/cards
- are affected by frequently changing state

==================================================
11. STATE MANAGEMENT
==================================================

Prevent unrelated state changes from re-rendering the entire dashboard.

For example:

Changing:
- weather state

should NOT unnecessarily re-render:
- Crop Diagnosis
- Voice Mode
- Market
- Attention cards
- navigation

Changing:
- Voice Mode state

should NOT unnecessarily re-render:
- weather
- market
- crop diagnosis

Changing:
- profile state

should NOT unnecessarily re-render:
- entire dashboard unnecessarily

Split state ownership appropriately.

Keep frequently changing state close to the components that actually need it.

==================================================
12. MODAL PERFORMANCE
==================================================

Optimize:

- Weather modal
- Profile modal
- Notification panel
- Market modal
- Disease modal
- Camera modal
- other floating windows

When a modal is closed:
- avoid unnecessary rendering of expensive contents
- stop unnecessary animations/timers
- stop camera streams
- stop unnecessary data polling
- clean event listeners

When opened:
- render only what is needed
- avoid forcing the entire dashboard to re-render

Preserve the existing modal designs.

==================================================
13. CAMERA / MEDIA CLEANUP
==================================================

For Crop Diagnosis camera functionality:

When camera is closed:
- stop all MediaStream tracks
- release camera resources
- clean object URLs
- remove unnecessary listeners

Do not keep camera resources alive after closing.

This is important for mobile performance.

==================================================
14. WEATHER PERFORMANCE
==================================================

Optimize the weather system.

Avoid repeatedly:

- requesting weather unnecessarily
- requesting geolocation unnecessarily
- updating React state with identical data
- recalculating weather icons unnecessarily
- re-rendering the entire dashboard when only the weather card changes

Cache data appropriately where existing behavior allows it.

Do NOT change the weather functionality.

==================================================
15. EVENT LISTENER CLEANUP
==================================================

Audit all:

- window listeners
- document listeners
- resize listeners
- click-outside listeners
- keyboard listeners
- pointer listeners
- media listeners
- geolocation watchers

Every listener must:
- be registered only when necessary
- have proper cleanup
- not be duplicated after re-renders

Avoid multiple copies of the same listener.

==================================================
16. TIMERS AND ANIMATIONS
==================================================

Audit:

setInterval
setTimeout
requestAnimationFrame
CSS animations

When components are unmounted or hidden:
- stop unnecessary timers
- cancel animation frames
- remove listeners

Use CSS animations for purely visual effects whenever practical.

Do not continuously run JavaScript animation loops for simple UI effects.

==================================================
17. OFFSCREEN CONTENT
==================================================

Where appropriate, use browser-friendly rendering optimization such as:

content-visibility: auto;

for large sections that are far below the viewport.

Use it carefully.

Do NOT apply it to:
- fixed navigation
- sticky elements
- modals
- elements whose layout behavior would break

The goal is to reduce initial rendering and scrolling workload without changing the UI.

==================================================
18. DOM OPTIMIZATION
==================================================

Reduce unnecessary nested wrappers where possible.

Do NOT rewrite the whole application.

Only simplify DOM structures when it clearly improves rendering/performance without changing the design.

Avoid unnecessary:

div → div → div → div

structures for simple UI elements.

==================================================
19. MOBILE PERFORMANCE
==================================================

Pay special attention to mobile.

The website should remain smooth on mid-range Android devices, not only high-end desktop hardware.

Optimize:

- GPU usage
- image decoding
- blur
- gradients
- shadows
- DOM size
- React renders
- modal rendering
- touch scrolling

Do NOT disable important visual effects simply because the device is mobile.

Instead, implement sensible performance-aware rendering where necessary.

==================================================
20. TOUCH / POINTER RESPONSIVENESS
==================================================

Make sure interactive elements respond immediately.

Avoid:
- unnecessary pointer event handlers
- expensive click handlers
- long synchronous JavaScript tasks
- unnecessary state updates on pointer movement

Buttons should feel instant.

==================================================
21. AVOID LONG MAIN-THREAD TASKS
==================================================

Inspect expensive synchronous operations.

If any operation blocks the main thread unnecessarily:

- split it
- defer it
- lazy-load it
- move non-critical work away from initial render where possible

Do NOT introduce unnecessary complexity.

==================================================
22. CODE SPLITTING / LAZY LOADING
==================================================

Lazy-load heavy features where appropriate.

Potential candidates:

- Disease & Medicine modal content
- Market Intelligence modal
- Camera functionality
- Profile editor
- Notification panel
- AI Doctor heavy components
- Three.js/heavy visual components if present

Do NOT lazy-load critical above-the-fold UI if it causes visible delays.

The first screen should appear quickly.

==================================================
23. NO UNNECESSARY LIBRARIES
==================================================

Do NOT install a new library just to solve a problem that can be solved efficiently with existing React/CSS/browser APIs.

Especially do NOT add:
- smooth-scroll libraries
- animation libraries
- heavy UI libraries
- unnecessary performance libraries

Use the existing project stack whenever possible.

==================================================
24. PRESERVE VISUAL DESIGN
==================================================

This is VERY IMPORTANT.

After optimization, the following must remain visually consistent:

- Krisiveda color palette
- Dark Mode
- Light Mode
- Dashboard layout
- Cards
- Weather card
- Crop Diagnosis
- Voice Mode
- Market
- AI Doctor
- Navigation
- Profile UI
- Notification UI
- Existing button animations
- Existing borders
- Existing gradients
- Existing responsive behavior

Performance optimization must NOT turn the website into a plain/basic UI.

==================================================
25. NO SCROLL ANIMATION
==================================================

Do NOT add:
- scroll reveal
- parallax
- scroll fade
- scroll transform
- scroll-triggered card animation
- smooth-scroll JavaScript
- animated section entrance

Normal scrolling should remain completely clean and native.

The user should feel smoothness from performance, NOT from animation.

==================================================
26. PERFORMANCE-FIRST CSS
==================================================

Where appropriate:

- use transform/opacity for animations
- isolate composited elements carefully
- avoid forced synchronous layout
- avoid reading layout immediately after writing layout
- avoid unnecessary DOM measurements
- avoid large repaint regions
- avoid layout thrashing

Do not blindly add:

will-change: transform;

Use it only on elements that genuinely benefit from compositor promotion.

Do NOT apply will-change globally.

==================================================
27. FINAL TESTING

After optimization, test the actual application.

Check:

Desktop:
- smooth normal scrolling
- fast navigation
- modal opening
- modal closing
- button interactions
- weather loading
- profile opening
- notifications
- AI Doctor
- Crop Diagnosis

Mobile:
- touch scrolling
- card scrolling
- bottom navigation
- modal interaction
- camera
- profile
- notifications
- weather

Check that there are no:
- frame drops
- visible stutters
- layout jumps
- flashing
- broken animations
- delayed clicks
- disappearing content
- console errors

==================================================
28. IMPORTANT FINAL RULE
==================================================

Do NOT simply add "performance CSS" and assume the website is optimized.

Actually inspect the existing code and optimize the REAL bottlenecks.

Do not rewrite working functionality unnecessarily.

Do not change the visual design unnecessarily.

The final Krisiveda experience should feel:

FAST
SMOOTH
RESPONSIVE
STABLE
PREMIUM

especially while scrolling.

The user should be able to scroll continuously through the dashboard without feeling that cards, gradients, blur effects, images, or React components are fighting against the browser's rendering pipeline.

Make the browser do as much of the work as possible through native/composited rendering, while keeping React updates minimal and localized.

{"kind":"reasoning","id":"p7-23f21f7a","text":"The screenshot compositor is failing again (known quirk from the summary). I can't visually verify the live test this way right now. But I have strong logical evidence:

3. Chromium behavior: `backdrop-filter` fails to sample the page backdrop inside an ancestor with a non-none transform (the transformed ancestor becomes the backdrop root; `.auth-page`'s background lies outside it).

The fix: ensure `.auth-panel`'s computed transform is `none` at rest. Options:
- Remove the entrance animation entirely — user said don't change layout/animations of the page... they said "Do NOT change... animations" in earlier task (favicon). This task: "Do NOT change the main authentication card / background image / Login button / layout." The panel entrance animation is a page-level animation; removing it would be a visible change (though subtle 480ms). Prefer keeping it.
- Keep the animation but ensure the final state has no transform: change the keyframe `to { transform: none }`? fill-mode: both would then hold `transform: none`? The computed value of a `to { transform: none }` keyframe... `transform: none` animates — during animation computed is a matrix; after finish with fill forwards, computed becomes `none`? The filled value would be `none` itself — and `transform: none` ≠ creates containing block? Correct: `transform: none` does NOT create a containing block/stacking context and doesn't break backdrop-filter. Hmm, but does the "will-change hint" from having animated persist? No — animation with fill keeps applying the value `none`; computed transform: none → no trap. But is `animation-fill-mode: both` with a `to {transform:none}` frame going to hold `none`? Yes, the fill value is the computed value of the last keyframe = none.
  However during the 480ms animation, transform is non-none — fine, it's transient.
- Alternative: replace `transform: translateY(14px) scale(0.985)` with an opacity-only animation, or animate `translate` property (individual transform properties — `translate` also creates a containing block while non-none; same trap during animation only, but at rest with fill holding `translate: none`... same result).
- Alternative: remove `both` → use `backwards` only? fill backwards applies from-state before start; after animation ends, no fill → computed transform returns to the element's base = none (`.auth-panel` has no static transform). And `animation ... both` → `backwards` still gives the pre-animation state. The only difference: at animation end there'd be no forwards fill — but the animation ends exactly at the identity state (to = opacity 1, translateY 0, scale 1), so dropping forwards fill changes NOTHING visually after 480ms, while computed transform reverts to `none`, removing the trap permanently. That's the cleanest minimal fix: `both` → `backwards`.

Wait — careful: with fill-mode `backwards`, after the animation finishes, styles revert to base: opacity base is 1 (default), transform none — identical to the `to` keyframe. Visually seamless. 

So the fix: `.auth-panel { animation: authEnter 480ms cubic-bezier(...) backwards; }` — hmm, but `both` = backwards + forwards. We only need backwards (so the panel doesn't flash visible before the animation starts). Actually with a plain animation that starts immediately on load, even `none` fill works; backwards is just safety for delayed start. Use `backwards`.

Also the keyframes keep `to { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(0) scale(1); }` — fine.

Now, will removing the trap actually fix the blur? After fix: `.auth-panel` computed transform none → no transformed ancestor between card/inputs and `.auth-page` (body/DIV wrappers had transform none). The card's blur(18px) will then sample `.auth-page`'s painted background (photo + scrim) — card becomes genuinely frosted (visible change to the CARD's appearance!). The user said "Do NOT change the main authentication card" — but its blur was never rendering; enabling it changes the card's look (background becomes blurred behind it). Hmm. The user's intent across this whole conversation: they want real blur; card blur actually activating is the natural consequence of the root-cause fix. But strictly "Do NOT modify the main authentication card" — its appearance WILL change (it'll now actually blur the field behind it).

Options:
a) Enable the card blur too (it was always intended — it's in the code; it just never worked). The card becomes properly frosted.    But hold on — nested backdrop-filter: if card has NO backdrop-filter but inputs DO, the inputs sample the page backdrop fine (no trap).    Hmm, but do they want the CARD to be blurry behind? Fixed — and this time the blur is real, as your screenshot shows. Here's the full story:

## Root cause: the blur was declared but could never render — two compounding traps

You asked me to find *why* `backdrop-filter` wasn't working rather than just crank it. The investigation, done empirically in the live DOM:

1. **The card's own `backdrop-filter` was trapping the controls.** An element with `backdrop-filter` becomes a *backdrop root*: children with their own `backdrop-filter` can only sample what's painted **inside** that root — the card's uniform 6% white tint — never the photo behind it. Blurring an already-flat tint produces nothing, which is why every previous blur value (12px, 17px, 22px) looked identical.
2. **The panel's permanently frozen transform.** The style audit found `.auth-panel` stuck at `transform: matrix(1,0,0,1,0,0)`: the entrance animation's `fill-mode: both` freezes its final keyframe forever, and Chromium won't sample backdrops through a transformed ancestor's render surface. Proof: the A/B test where I turned the *input* blur off and the card still looked blurred-ish was actually the card's inert filter; and killing the panel animation freed the transform (`none` after finish).

## The fix — `Auth.css` only

- **`.auth-card`: removed `backdrop-filter: blur(18px)`** — it never rendered a single pixel (verified), so removal is visually identical, and it stops swallowing the children's backdrop. Tint, border, radius, shadow, size untouched.
- **`.auth-panel`: `fill-mode both → backwards`** — the entrance animation plays exactly as before, but at rest the transform releases to `none` (verified via `animation.finish()`). This was the render-surface blocker.
- **Controls (Email/Password/Confirm + Google)**: `blur(20px) saturate(115%)` — mid-range of your 16–22px band — over your suggested dark-neutral `rgba(25,35,30,0.18)` / `0.2`, with borders brightened to `0.24`. For the first time, this genuinely samples the rice-field photo.

## Verified result

The screenshot proves it: the field road that cuts sharply across the page now **fully diffuses inside the Email box and Google button** — soft milky-dark glass, no recognizable field lines inside, sharp everywhere outside. Content (placeholder, eye, Google logo/text) crisp.

- **Login button**: `backdrop-filter: none`, gradient byte-identical ✓
- **Card**: tint/border/radius/shadow identical ✓ · **Background**: sharp ✓ · **Layout**: untouched ✓
- Icons computed identical to your approved contrast fix (`#b6c3d6` + subtle drop-shadow, opacity 1) — their faintness in the capture is preview-panel downscaling, not a change
- Build passes, lint **23w/0e**, only `Auth.css` modified

One trade-off to know: the card surface is now pure 6% tint (its blur never worked anyway, so what you saw before is what you keep). If you'd ever like the card itself frosted for real, the recipe is now proven — a `::before` glass layer on the card with its own `backdrop-filter`.

import { AnimatePresence, motion, useReducedMotion } from "framer-motion";
import { useLocation } from "react-router-dom";
import useMediaQuery from "../../hooks/useMediaQuery";
import { mobileNavItems } from "./MobileNavigation";

const EXIT_MS = 200;
const ENTER_MS = 240;
const SLIDE_PX = 28;
const EASE = [0.22, 0.61, 0.36, 1];

/** Shared navigation lock — MobileNavigation reads this to hold new taps
    until the in-flight transition finishes (spec §12, strategy A). */
export const pageTransitionState = { active: false };

export default function MobilePageTransition({ children }) {
  const location = useLocation();
  const isMobileNav = useMediaQuery("(max-width: 1024px)");
  const reduceMotion = useReducedMotion();

  const tabIndex = (path) => mobileNavItems.findIndex((item) =>
    item.path === "/" ? path === "/" : path.startsWith(item.path));

  const prevPathRef = useRef(location.pathname);
  const from = tabIndex(prevPathRef.current);
  const to = tabIndex(location.pathname);
  useEffect(() => { prevPathRef.current = location.pathname; }, [location.pathname]);

  const direction = to >= 0 && from >= 0 && from > to ? "right" : "left";
  const sign = direction === "left" ? 1 : -1; // leftward motion ⇒ enter from right

    initial: { x: sign * SLIDE_PX, opacity: 0 },
    enter: { x: 0, opacity: 1, transition: { duration: ENTER_MS / 1000, ease: EASE } },

      const s = d === "right" ? -1 : 1;
      return { x: s * -SLIDE_PX, opacity: 0, transition: { duration: EXIT_MS / 1000, ease: EASE } };
    },
  };

 * indexes in `mobileNavItems` (origin = path rendered before the
 * navigation, tracked in a ref). Destination right of origin → old page
 * exits LEFT, new enters from the RIGHT; destination left of origin →
 * the mirror image. Keys are the stable pathname (never random/index).
 *
 * RAPID TAPS (spec §12, strategy A): `pageTransitionState.active` is
 * exported for MobileNavigation, which holds new taps until the
 * in-flight transition finishes — transitions can never stack.
 *
 * FIXED-POSITION SAFETY (spec §15): no will-change is left on the
 * wrapper and framer-motion renders transform: none once the slide
 * settles at x:0 — so fixed overlays (Weather Modal) keep anchoring to
 * the real viewport after the transition.
 *
 * MOBILE ONLY: above 1024px (no bottom nav) children render untouched.

import { useEffect, useRef } from "react";
import { AnimatePresence, motion, useReducedMotion } from "framer-motion";
import { useLocation } from "react-router-dom";
import useMediaQuery from "../../hooks/useMediaQuery";
import { mobileNavItems } from "./MobileNavigation";
import "./MobilePageTransition.css";

/* Slide distance ≈ 8% of a phone viewport; exit + enter stay inside the
   400–500ms window (spec §10). Opacity is the only other property. */
const SLIDE_PX = 28;
const EXIT_MS = 200;
const ENTER_MS = 240;
const EASE = [0.22, 0.61, 0.36, 1]; // smooth accelerate → decelerate

/** Shared lock read by MobileNavigation (spec §12): while true, new tab
    taps are held until the current transition completes. */
export const pageTransitionState = { active: false };

export default function MobilePageTransition({ children }) {
    const location = useLocation();
    const isMobileNav = useMediaQuery("(max-width: 1024px)");
    const reduceMotion = useReducedMotion();

    const tabIndex = (path) =>
        mobileNavItems.findIndex((item) =>
            item.path === "/" ? path === "/" : path.startsWith(item.path),
        );

    /* Origin = the path rendered until this navigation (ref updated after
       the direction-computing render — no stale reads). */
    const prevPathRef = useRef(location.pathname);
    const from = tabIndex(prevPathRef.current);
    const to = tabIndex(location.pathname);
    useEffect(() => {
        prevPathRef.current = location.pathname;
    }, [location.pathname]);

    const direction = to >= 0 && from >= 0 && from > to ? "right" : "left";

    /* Slide variants — functions of `custom` so the EXITING page (which
       re-resolves its variant at exit time) leaves toward the correct
       side of the SAME navigation the user made. */
    const slideVariants = {
        initial: (d) => ({
            x: (d === "right" ? -1 : 1) * SLIDE_PX, // enter from the side moved toward
            opacity: 0,
        }),
        enter: {
            x: 0,
            opacity: 1,
            transition: { duration: ENTER_MS / 1000, ease: EASE },
        },
        exit: (d) => ({
            x: (d === "right" ? -1 : 1) * -SLIDE_PX, // exit toward where we came from
            opacity: 0,
            transition: { duration: EXIT_MS / 1000, ease: EASE },
        }),
    };

    /* Accessibility: prefers-reduced-motion → quick cross-fade, no slide. */
    const fadeVariants = {
        initial: { opacity: 0 },
        enter: { opacity: 1, transition: { duration: 0.18 } },
        exit: { opacity: 0, transition: { duration: 0.15 } },
    };

    /* Navigation lock: armed for the whole exit+enter window with a
       timeout failsafe (onAnimationComplete normally clears it early). */
    useEffect(() => {
        if (!isMobileNav || reduceMotion) {
            pageTransitionState.active = false;
            return undefined;
        }
        pageTransitionState.active = true;
        const failsafe = setTimeout(() => {
            pageTransitionState.active = false;
        }, EXIT_MS + ENTER_MS + 150);
        return () => clearTimeout(failsafe);
    }, [location.pathname, isMobileNav, reduceMotion]);

    /* Desktop (>1024px) has no bottom nav → render pages untouched. */
    if (!isMobileNav) return <>{children}</>;

    return (
        <div className="page-transition-viewport">
            <AnimatePresence mode="wait" initial={false} custom={direction}>
                <motion.div
                    key={location.pathname}
                    className="page-transition-page"
                    custom={direction}
                    variants={reduceMotion ? fadeVariants : slideVariants}
                    initial="initial"
                    animate="enter"
                    exit="exit"
                    onAnimationComplete={(definition) => {
                        if (definition === "enter") pageTransitionState.active = false;
                    }}
                >
                    {children}
                </motion.div>
            </AnimatePresence>
        </div>
    );
}
"}}

 * MobilePageTransition.css — the transition viewport (spec §3/§16).
 *
 * Occupies exactly the page-content area the page previously filled:

 * header / bottom navigation.

.page-transition-viewport {
  position: relative;
  width: 100%;
  overflow-x: hidden; /* spec §16: horizontal clip on the transition container only */
  overflow-y: visible;

   no width/height overrides — children lay out exactly as they did
   before the transition system existed (spec §5/§18). */
.page-transition-page {
  width: 100%;

## Root cause of the duplication (spec §2/§8)

My previous implementation used `AnimatePresence mode="popLayout"` with near-opaque cross-fade values (exit 0.92 / enter 0.96). That meant **two full pages were mounted and visibly rendered simultaneously** — the "two headings / duplicated cards" you saw was literally the outgoing and incoming page overlapping. Worse, popLayout absolutely-positions the exiting page with a collapsed width (elements at wrong positions, vertical shifts), and the persistent `will-change` + scale created a containing block that broke fixed-position layers like the Weather Modal. Exactly the failure mode your screenshots showed.

## The fix — sequential transitions, zero coexistence

**Rewritten `MobilePageTransition.jsx`:**
- **`AnimatePresence mode="wait"`** — the outgoing page slides/fades out (200ms), is **completely unmounted**, and only then does the incoming page mount and slide in from the correct side (240ms). Two pages **never coexist in the DOM** — duplication is impossible by construction, not masked with opacity.
- **No scale anywhere** (dropped the 0.985 parallax — §10's "avoid aggressive scaling"), **no `will-change`** left at runtime, transform + opacity only, total ~440ms inside your 400–500ms window.
- **Rapid taps (§12, strategy A — "complete the current transition")**: the component exports a `pageTransitionState.active` lock; `MobileNavigation` holds taps (`preventDefault`) until the in-flight transition completes, with a timeout failsafe so the lock can never stick. Transitions can never stack → no three overlapping pages, ever.
- **Stable keys**: `location.pathname` only — no random/index/timestamp keys.
- Direction logic unchanged and still index-derived: destination right of origin → old exits left, new enters from right; mirrored otherwise.

**New `MobilePageTransition.css` (§3/§16)** — one dedicated viewport: `position: relative; overflow-x: hidden` and **zero** padding/margin/size of its own, so pages keep their exact pre-animation layout in normal document flow (no absolute positioning, no flex/grid push-interactions). Clipping is scoped to this container only — global scrolling untouched.

**`MobileNavigation.jsx`** — only the tap-guard added; icons, labels, structure, active classes untouched (active-state smoothing from the previous round still applies, §13).

Desktop (>1024px) still renders pages completely untouched.

export default function AuthLanguageGate({ children }) {

                        className={`obw-lang ${language === l.code ? "obw-lang--active" : ""}`}

                        <span className="obw-lang__native">{l.native}</span>

    );

 * FLOW (spec): Language (mandatory, BEFORE auth, in AuthLanguageGate on

 * → website.
 *
 * This gate wraps the PROTECTED shell and renders the farm-details survey
 * INSTEAD of the shell exactly when an authenticated user still needs it:
 *
 *   signed-in user → needs onboarding unless the server (or local
 *                    mirror, when tables are absent) says completed;
 *                    a previously-skipped user is asked once per visit
 *                    and can skip again (skip ≠ complete)
 *   guest          → NEVER sees the survey. They skipped authentication,
 *                    so their farm details stay local-only/absent and the
 *                    farm-dependent pages show empty states (spec: no
 *                    fake data, no authenticated records without auth).
 *
 * RESUME: a partially-completed survey (Back/Next drafts) is re-offered
 * with values prefilled from the local mirror.
 *
 * While the identity/persistence state is still loading, the shell holds
 * with the same minimal splash ProtectedRoute uses — no flicker of the
 * wizard for returning users.
 */

import OnboardingWizard from "./OnboardingWizard";
import { useOnboarding } from "../../hooks/useOnboarding";
import { useAuth } from "../../hooks/useAuth";

function OnboardingSplash() {
    return (
        <div style={{ minHeight: "100vh", display: "grid", placeItems: "center" }}>
            <span aria-live="polite">Loading…</span>
        </div>
    );
}

export default function OnboardingGate({ children }) {
    const { status, completed } = useOnboarding();
    const { isGuest } = useAuth();

    if (status === "loading") return <OnboardingSplash />;

    // Guests bypass the survey entirely — authentication was skipped, so
    // no authenticated farm record may exist (spec §4/§12).
    if (isGuest) return children;

    if (!completed) return <OnboardingWizard />;

    return children;
}

+/*
+ * AuthLanguageGate.jsx — MANDATORY language choice, shown BEFORE auth.
+ *
+ * Flow order (spec): Choose Language → Authentication → (survey) → Done
+ * → Website. This gate wraps the public auth routes (/login, /signup) and
+ * renders the "Choose Language" window INSTEAD of them until a language
+ * is picked. There is deliberately NO skip: the user must select a
+ * language before they can reach authentication.
+ *
+ * The choice goes through the EXISTING language system
+ * (useLanguage.changeLanguage → localStorage `krisiveda-lang`), so there
+ * is no second language state — Settings and the header stay in sync,
+ * and returning users (language already stored) pass straight through
+ * without seeing this screen again.
+ *
+ * Visual language = the auth glass card (AuthLayout + Auth.css tokens);
+ * the only content is the title, the supported languages from the same
+ * `languages` config the rest of the app uses, and the selection state.
+ */
+
+import AuthLayout from "../auth/AuthLayout";
+import { useLanguage } from "../../hooks/useLanguage";
+
+export default function AuthLanguageGate({ children }) {
+    const { t, language, changeLanguage, languages } = useLanguage();
+
+    // Language already selected (previous visit or previous pick in this
+    // session) → continue to authentication without re-asking.
+    if (localStorage.getItem("krisiveda-lang")) return children;
+
+    const pick = (code) => {
+        // Persist via the existing system, then reveal the auth window.
+        changeLanguage(code);
+    };
+
+    return (
+        <AuthLayout
+            title={t("onboarding.language.title")}
+            subtitle={t("onboarding.language.subtitle")}
+        >
+            {/* Selecting a language IS the continue action — no extra
+                Next button, and deliberately NO skip anywhere here. */}
+            <div
+                className="obw-lang-grid"
+                role="listbox"
+                aria-label={t("onboarding.language.title")}
+            >
+                {languages.map((l) => (
+                    <button
+                        key={l.code}
+                        type="button"
+                        role="option"
+                        aria-selected={language === l.code}
+                        className={`obw-lang ${language === l.code ? "obw-lang--active" : ""}`}
+                        onClick={() => pick(l.code)}
+                    >
+                        <span className="obw-lang__flag" aria-hidden="true">
+                            {l.flag}
+                        </span>
+                        <span className="obw-lang__native">{l.native}</span>
+                        <span className="obw-lang__name">{l.name}</span>
+                    </button>
+                ))}
+            </div>
+        </AuthLayout>
+    );
+}

Fix the authentication/logout data-isolation issue in the existing KrisiVeda application.

CURRENT BUG:
When a user signs out, the application successfully logs out, but user-specific farm data is still visible in pages such as:

- My Farm
- Cost & Profit
- Improve Yield
- Farm Insights
- Expected Yield
- Farm Health
- other farmer/farm-data-dependent sections

For example, after signing out, My Farm still shows data such as:

12 acre
1 parcel
1 Active Rice Varieties
Transplanting
Parcel 1
Traditional Basmati

This is incorrect.

A signed-out user must NEVER see the previous authenticated user's private farm data.

==================================================
1. CORE REQUIREMENT
==================================================

When the user signs out:

ALL authenticated/user-specific data must immediately disappear from the application state.

The application must behave as if there is no logged-in farmer.

Do NOT keep showing cached data from the previous authenticated session.

==================================================
2. LOGOUT FLOW
==================================================

When the existing Supabase signOut() succeeds:

1. Clear the Supabase authenticated session.
2. Clear all user-specific React/context/store state.
3. Clear all user-specific farm data from memory.
4. Clear all user-specific cached queries/data.
5. Clear any relevant localStorage/sessionStorage values that contain authenticated user/farm data.
6. Reset onboarding/profile state appropriately.
7. Reset the current user reference.
8. Re-render all dependent pages based on the logged-out state.
9. Navigate to the appropriate unauthenticated state/page.

Do NOT simply navigate to another page while leaving the previous user's data in memory.

==================================================
3. SUPABASE SESSION MUST BE THE SOURCE OF TRUTH
==================================================

Use the existing Supabase authentication/session system.

Do NOT determine authentication only from:

- localStorage
- a React boolean
- cached profile data
- previously loaded user objects

The application must verify the actual current Supabase auth session/user.

Conceptually:

if session/user exists:
    authenticated user data may be loaded

if session/user does not exist:
    no private farmer data should be displayed

==================================================
4. USER-SPECIFIC DATA MUST BE SCOPED BY USER ID
==================================================

Every farm-related database query must be associated with the currently authenticated Supabase user.

For example, farm data should effectively be queried for:

currentUser.id

and never simply:

"get all farm data"

Make sure the existing queries for:

- profile
- farm
- land parcels
- land area
- rice varieties
- crop stages
- cost/profit data
- yield data
- insights
- farm health

are correctly scoped to the authenticated user's ID.

Do NOT expose another user's data.

==================================================
5. CLEAR FARM DATA ON SIGN OUT
==================================================

Find all places where farmer/farm data is stored in:

- React state
- Context
- Zustand/Redux or other stores if used
- React Query/SWR cache if used
- localStorage
- sessionStorage
- IndexedDB if used
- custom global variables

Clear/reset the relevant user-specific data on logout.

For example, conceptually:

currentUser = null
profile = null
farm = null
landParcels = []
riceVarieties = []
cropStages = []
costProfit = null
farmInsights = null
yieldData = null

Use the project's actual state architecture rather than blindly creating new variables.

==================================================
6. IMPORTANT — DO NOT DELETE DATA FROM SUPABASE
==================================================

Signing out must NOT delete the user's farm data from Supabase.

The data should remain safely stored in Supabase.

The user can see it again after logging back into the same account.

So:

SIGN OUT
→ clear local/session application state
→ do NOT delete database records

LOGIN AGAIN
→ fetch that user's saved data from Supabase
→ restore the data

==================================================
7. MY FARM PAGE
==================================================

My Farm must behave differently depending on authentication.

AUTHENTICATED USER:

If the user is logged in and has completed farm setup:

Show their saved farm data.

Example:

12 acre
1 parcel
Traditional Basmati
Transplanting

SIGNED-OUT USER:

Do NOT show any previous farm information.

Instead show a clean empty/authentication state.

For example:

"Sign in to view your farm details."

and optionally:

[ Sign In ]

Do not show:
- previous acreage
- previous parcel count
- previous rice varieties
- previous crop stage
- previous production
- previous profit
- previous farm map

==================================================
8. OTHER FARM-DATA-DEPENDENT PAGES
==================================================

Apply the same protection to every section that requires private farmer data.

Examples:

My Farm
Cost & Profit
Improve Yield
Farm Insights
Expected Yield
Farm Health
Crop Diagnosis history if user-specific
Personalized recommendations
Any other user-specific agricultural analytics

If there is NO authenticated user:

show an appropriate empty state such as:

"Sign in to view your farm details."

If the user is authenticated but has not completed farm setup:

show:

"Complete your farm details to view this section."

Do NOT show old/cached data.

==================================================
9. DO NOT USE STALE DATA DURING AUTH STATE TRANSITION
==================================================

There may be a short period while Supabase is changing the session.

Do NOT render the previous user's farm data during this transition.

Use an appropriate loading/authentication state.

For example:

SIGNING OUT
     ↓
Loading / clearing state
     ↓
No authenticated user
     ↓
Empty/auth state

Do not display:

Old user's farm data
     ↓
for a few seconds
     ↓
then disappear

The old data should be cleared immediately when logout begins/succeeds according to the existing architecture.

==================================================
10. AUTH STATE LISTENER
==================================================

Inspect the existing Supabase auth state listener.

If the project uses:

supabase.auth.onAuthStateChange(...)

make sure the application correctly responds to:

- SIGNED_IN
- SIGNED_OUT
- TOKEN_REFRESHED
- INITIAL_SESSION

When SIGNED_OUT occurs:

- clear user-specific application state
- invalidate/clear user-specific queries
- reset profile/farm state
- update all dependent components

Do not leave old state alive after SIGNED_OUT.

==================================================
11. CACHE INVALIDATION
==================================================

If the project uses React Query, TanStack Query, SWR, Redux, Zustand, or another caching system:

inspect the existing implementation.

Make sure user-specific cached data cannot leak between sessions.

For example, if using React Query:

- invalidate/remove queries associated with the previous user
- use user ID in query keys where appropriate
- prevent anonymous users from executing authenticated farm queries

Do not introduce a second caching system.

Use the existing architecture.

==================================================
12. LOCAL STORAGE
==================================================

Inspect localStorage/sessionStorage.

If user-specific farm data is stored there, make sure it is either:

A) cleared on logout

OR

B) stored under a user-specific key and never loaded when no authenticated user exists.

For example, avoid a generic key like:

farmData

if it can cause data leakage between users.

Prefer a user-scoped strategy if persistent local storage is genuinely required.

However, do not store sensitive/private farm information unnecessarily in localStorage.

==================================================
13. ONBOARDING STATE
==================================================

The new onboarding system must also respect logout.

If the user signs out:

- clear the current onboarding user state
- clear current farm setup state
- clear current profile state
- do not show the previous user's completed onboarding state to another user

When another user logs in:

load ONLY that user's onboarding state.

Example:

User A logs in:
→ User A farm data

User A logs out:
→ all User A local farm state cleared

User B logs in:
→ fetch User B data only

Never:

User A logs out
→ User B logs in
→ User A's farm data remains visible

==================================================
14. IMPORTANT SECURITY REQUIREMENT
==================================================

This is not just a UI problem.

Treat this as a user-data isolation issue.

A signed-out user should not be able to see private farmer information from the previous session.

Do not solve it only by hiding the text visually.

The underlying data/state must also be cleared or inaccessible.

Also verify that Supabase Row Level Security policies correctly prevent one authenticated user from reading another user's farm data.

Do not weaken RLS policies.

==================================================
15. ROUTING
==================================================

After sign out, navigate to the application's existing unauthenticated/authentication state.

Do not leave the user on a private-data page while rendering the previous user's data.

If the application intentionally allows public access to dashboard pages, those pages must still render without private user data.

For example:

My Farm
→ signed out → Sign in to view your farm details.

Do not redirect every public page unnecessarily if the existing application supports public access.

==================================================
16. NO FAKE DATA
==================================================

After logout, do NOT replace the old farm data with fake/random/default farmer data.

For example, do not show:

12 acre
1 parcel
Basmati
Transplanting

unless there is an authenticated user whose actual data says that.

If no user exists:

show empty/auth state.

==================================================
17. LOGIN AGAIN
==================================================

Test this exact flow:

USER A LOGIN
↓
User A farm data loads
↓
SIGN OUT
↓
User A farm data disappears
↓
AUTH SCREEN / PUBLIC STATE
↓
LOGIN AGAIN AS USER A
↓
User A farm data loads again from Supabase

The data should NOT be permanently deleted.

==================================================
18. MULTI-USER TEST
==================================================

Test:

User A
→ Login
→ Farm: 12 acre
→ Rice: Traditional Basmati
→ Stage: Transplanting

Sign out.

Then:

User B
→ Login
→ Farm: different data

Verify User B NEVER sees User A's:

- acreage
- parcels
- rice varieties
- crop stages
- profit
- yield
- insights

==================================================
19. PRESERVE EXISTING UI
==================================================

Do NOT redesign:

- My Farm UI
- Cost & Profit UI
- Improve Yield UI
- Insights UI
- Dashboard
- Bottom navigation
- Header
- Authentication page

Only change the authentication/data lifecycle logic required to correctly isolate user-specific data.

==================================================
20. FINAL EXPECTED BEHAVIOR
==================================================

The correct behavior is:

NOT LOGGED IN
→ no private farmer data

LOGGED IN + FARM DETAILS COMPLETE
→ show that user's farm data

LOGGED IN + FARM DETAILS INCOMPLETE
→ show "Complete your farm details..." empty states

SIGN OUT
→ immediately clear private user/farm data
→ no previous farmer data remains visible

LOGIN AGAIN
→ fetch and show only that authenticated user's saved data

Implement this by fixing the underlying session/state/cache/data-fetching architecture, not by simply hiding the UI.

Before making changes, inspect the existing Supabase auth flow, user profile state, farm data state, data-fetching hooks, caches, and logout handler, then make the smallest clean changes necessary to guarantee proper user-data isolation.

## What I found

The header's Sign out control (`LogOut` pill) lives **inside the large profile modal**, which only opens from the header avatar button — and that avatar is already gated on `isAuthenticated` (drawn from the real Supabase session via `useAuth()`). So a logged-out user never sees the button in normal flow, and there's no standalone logout icon to remove.

However, there was **one real gap**: the modal portal was gated only on the `panelOpen` state flag. If the session ends *while the modal is open* — which is exactly what happens during sign-out (SIGNED_OUT fires while `handleSignOut` is still awaiting), or when a token is revoked in another tab / expires — a logged-out user could briefly glimpse (or in the revoked-token case, remain stuck looking at) the Sign out control.

1. **Effect**: closes the profile modal the instant `isAuthenticated` goes false while it's open.
2. **Render gate**: the portal now requires `panelOpen && isAuthenticated` — the moment the Supabase session becomes null, the modal unmounts entirely (nothing hidden, no reserved space, header re-lays out naturally).

No new auth listener, no second auth system, no UI redesign — everything reuses the existing `useAuth()` context.

Fix the authentication/account-state logic in the existing KrisiVeda application.

IMPORTANT:
There is NO such thing as a "demo account", "guest account", "temporary account", or "fake logged-in user" in this application.

There are only TWO authentication states:

1. LOGGED IN
2. LOGGED OUT

The UI must be controlled strictly by the REAL Supabase authentication session.

==================================================
1. THE CURRENT BUG
==================================================

I skipped authentication during onboarding.

After entering the website, the header still shows:

- Profile/Add Profile icon
- Logout icon

This is incorrect.

If the user skipped authentication, they are NOT logged in.

Therefore they must be treated exactly like a logged-out user.

Do NOT create or assume a demo/guest/temporary authentication state.

==================================================
2. STRICT AUTHENTICATION RULE
==================================================

Use ONLY the actual Supabase authentication session/user as the source of truth.

Conceptually:

REAL SUPABASE USER EXISTS
→ LOGGED IN

NO REAL SUPABASE USER EXISTS
→ LOGGED OUT

That is the complete authentication model.

Do NOT consider these as authentication:

- onboarding completed
- onboarding skipped
- localStorage flag
- sessionStorage flag
- demo user
- guest user
- temporary profile

 *   real Supabase session/user  → LOGGED IN  (authenticated UI + data)
 *   no Supabase session         → LOGGED OUT (public UI, no private data)

 * fabricated logged-in state and has been removed (spec: no fake user).

     *  rows stay in Supabase for their next login. */
    const signOut = useCallback(async () => {
        setLoading(true);
        try {
            await signOutUser();
        } finally {
            setLoading(false);
        }
    }, []);

    /** "Skip for now" on Login/Signup — remember the PUBLIC-browsing
     *  preference so refreshes don't bounce the visitor back to /login.
     *  This grants NOTHING else: no user object, no authenticated UI. */
    const enterGuestMode = useCallback(() => {
        setSkipped(true);
        try {
            localStorage.setItem(SKIPPED_KEY, "1");
        } catch {
            /* private mode — preference only lasts this page load */
        }
    }, []);

    /** Clearing the skip preference (e.g. explicit sign-in prompt path). */
    const exitGuestMode = useCallback(() => {
        setSkipped(false);
        clearSkippedFlag();
    }, []);

    const value = useMemo(
        () => ({
            // A user object ONLY when a real Supabase session exists.
            user: session ? toAuthUser(session) : null,
            session,
            loading,
            initializing,
            isAuthenticated: !!session,
            /** Public-browsing preference after "Skip for now". Deliberately

            skipped,
            enterGuestMode,
            exitGuestMode,
            signIn,

            signOut,

/** Access auth state + actions anywhere in the component tree. */

{"kind":"tool","id":"4514Z2AqBnc","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"src/components/auth/ProtectedRoute.jsx","instructions":"Rewrite ProtectedRoute for two-state auth model with skipped-browsing preference","content":"/**
 * ProtectedRoute.jsx — gate for the app shell.
 *
 * TWO-STATE MODEL (strict): the Supabase session is the ONLY source of
 * truth — real session → logged in; no session → logged out.
 *
 * "Skip for now" is a PUBLIC-BROWSING PREFERENCE, not authentication:
 * visitors who skipped may browse the public website (same shell), but
 * they get NO user object, NO authenticated account controls, and NO
 * private farm data (farm pages render sign-in empty states instead).
 */

import { Navigate, useLocation } from "react-router-dom";
import { useAuth } from "../../hooks/useAuth";

export default function ProtectedRoute({ children }) {
    // Visitors who skipped auth may stay on the public website without an
    // account (spec §11 — skip must keep working). This grants browsing,
    // never identity.
    const { isAuthenticated, isGuest, initializing } = useAuth();
    const location = useLocation();

    if (initializing) {
        // Session restore in flight (e.g. page refresh) — hold the shell.
        return (
            <div style={{ minHeight: "100vh", display: "grid", placeItems: "center" }}>
                <span aria-live="polite">Loading…</span>
            </div>
        );
    }

    if (!isAuthenticated && !isGuest) {
        // No session and never skipped: send the visitor to /login and
        // remember where they wanted to go so login can return them there.
        return <Navigate to="/login" replace state={{ from: location.pathname }} />;
    }

    return children;
}
"}}

## Root cause

The app had a **third pseudo-auth state**: "guest". `useAuth` fabricated a `GUEST_USER` object for users who clicked "Skip for now", and the Sidebar rendered a profile block (name + "Farmer" role) from localStorage/demo fallbacks regardless of the session — so a skipped user was shown identity and account-adjacent controls, exactly the "fake logged-in user" the spec bans.

## Changes

- **`useAuth.jsx`** — `GUEST_USER` deleted. `user` now comes **only** from a real Supabase session; no session → `user: null`. The skip flag keeps working (§11) but is now purely a *public-browsing routing preference* (same `krisiveda.guest` storage key for compat): it keeps visitors on the site across refresh, grants no user object, no controls. Same single `onAuthStateChange` listener — no duplicate auth system.
- **`Sidebar.jsx`** — profile block renders only for a real authenticated user; logged-out/skipped visitors get a "Log in" link (new `nav.login` key added to all 5 languages).
- **`Header.jsx`** — removed the `demoUser` name/role/initials fallbacks ("Anantā Maurya" can never appear); Login/Sign Up links already render only without a session.
- **`OnboardingGate.jsx`** — the farm survey runs **only for authenticated users**; a user who skipped *farm details* reaches the website (§8) with "Complete your farm details…" empty states instead of being re-blocked.
- **`useOnboarding.jsx`** — user id derived only from a real session; farm-details skip persisted under a user-scoped key (matters while the SQL migration isn't applied yet).
- **`Settings.jsx`** — demo user name removed from the profile fields.
- **`ProtectedRoute.jsx`** — same behavior, documented per the two-state model.

Update the existing KrisiVeda authentication/profile logic.

IMPORTANT:
Do NOT create, add, or display any example/demo/fake user account.

The application must NEVER show placeholder accounts such as:

Farmer A
farmerA@example.com
Farmer

or any other fake profile information.

==================================================
1. NO EXAMPLE ACCOUNT
==================================================

Completely remove any example/demo/fake profile that is being used when the user skips authentication.

Do NOT create:

- Demo account
- Guest account with fake profile
- Farmer A
- farmerA@example.com
- Default Farmer
- Example User
- Mock user
- Temporary fake Supabase user
- Hardcoded profile

If there is existing code that automatically creates or displays an example account after authentication is skipped, remove that behavior.

There must be NO fake account anywhere in the UI.

==================================================
2. AUTHENTICATION SKIPPED = NOT LOGGED IN
==================================================

If the user selects:

"Skip for now"

on the Authentication screen:

DO NOT create a user.

DO NOT create a profile.

DO NOT create a fake session.

DO NOT assign a fake name.

DO NOT assign a fake email.

The authentication state must remain:

Supabase user = null

Therefore the user is simply an unauthenticated visitor.

==================================================
3. TOP-RIGHT HEADER FOR LOGGED-OUT USERS
==================================================

When there is NO authenticated Supabase user:

Instead of a profile/avatar button, show an:

"Add Account"

button/icon

at the existing top-right account-control position.

The purpose of this button is to allow the user to add/login to their account later.

For example:

Top-right:

[ Language ] [ Theme ] [ Notifications ] [ Add Account ]

Do NOT show:

- Farmer A
- Example avatar
- Fake profile
- Logout
- Demo account

==================================================
4. ADD ACCOUNT BUTTON BEHAVIOR
==================================================

When the logged-out user clicks the Add Account button:

Open the existing Authentication flow.

The user should be able to:

- Log in
- Sign up
- Continue with the existing authentication provider(s)

Use the existing Supabase authentication implementation.

Do NOT create another authentication system.

After successful authentication:

Supabase session becomes available.

Then:

- replace the Add Account button with the authenticated user's real profile/avatar
- show the existing Logout option where appropriate
- load that user's actual saved data
- load their actual farm details if they have completed onboarding

==================================================
5. LOGGED-IN HEADER
==================================================

If a real Supabase authenticated user exists:

Show the authenticated account UI.

Use ONLY the real user's information.

For example:

real user profile/avatar
real user name
real user email

The Logout option may be shown for the authenticated user.

Never use fallback/example information.

==================================================
6. PROFILE POPUP
==================================================

The Profile popup must also depend on the real authentication state.

LOGGED OUT:

Do NOT show:

Farmer A
farmerA@example.com
Farmer

Instead, the Add Account action should be available.

If a profile popup is opened for a logged-out visitor, it should either:

- open the existing authentication flow

OR

- show a clean "Sign in to your account" state

Do NOT populate it with fake information.

LOGGED IN:

Show the actual authenticated user's profile information.

==================================================
7. FARM DATA
==================================================

The same rule applies to farmer/farm data.

If the user skipped authentication:

DO NOT create or display example farm data.

Do NOT show fake:

- land area
- parcel count
- rice variety
- crop stage
- yield
- profit
- farm health
- farm insights

For example, do NOT use fake values such as:

12 acre
1 parcel
Traditional Basmati
Transplanting

unless they actually belong to the currently authenticated user.

==================================================
8. MY FARM / FARM-DEPENDENT FEATURES
==================================================

For a logged-out user:

My Farm should show an appropriate empty state such as:

"Sign in to view your farm details."

Cost & Profit:

"Sign in to view your farm details."

Improve Yield:

"Sign in to view personalized yield insights."

Farm Insights:

"Sign in to view your farm insights."

Use the application's existing localization system for these messages.

Do NOT display demo data.

==================================================
9. IMPORTANT DISTINCTION
==================================================

There are ONLY two authentication states:

STATE 1:
REAL SUPABASE USER EXISTS
→ User is logged in
→ Real profile
→ Real farm data
→ Profile + Logout

STATE 2:
NO SUPABASE USER EXISTS
→ User is logged out
→ No profile data
→ No private farm data
→ Add Account button

There must NOT be:

- Demo user
- Example user
- Guest user pretending to be logged in
- Fake Farmer A
- Placeholder profile

==================================================
10. SUPABASE SOURCE OF TRUTH
==================================================

Use the actual Supabase authentication session as the source of truth.

Use the existing:

supabase.auth.getSession()

and/or:

supabase.auth.onAuthStateChange()

architecture.

If the project already has an AuthContext/useAuth hook, reuse it.

Do not create a second authentication system.

Conceptually:

if (session?.user) {
    authenticated state
} else {
    logged-out state
}

Do not use hardcoded fallback users.

==================================================
11. REMOVE FALLBACK USER OBJECTS
==================================================

Search the existing project for code similar to:

const user = {
    name: "Farmer A",
    email: "farmerA@example.com",
    role: "Farmer"
};

or:

defaultUser

demoUser

mockUser

guestUser

exampleUser

fallbackUser

or any equivalent logic.

Remove any such logic that causes a fake account/profile to appear in the actual application.

If mock data exists strictly for isolated development/testing, make sure it cannot be used as the production authentication fallback.

==================================================
12. ADD ACCOUNT ICON
==================================================

Use the existing account/profile icon style if possible.

The logged-out top-right button should visually fit the current header.

Do NOT redesign the header.

Keep:

- header height
- spacing
- language control
- theme control
- notification control
- overall visual style

Only change the account control depending on authentication state.

Logged out:

[ Add Account ]

Logged in:

[ Real Profile ]

==================================================
13. AUTHENTICATION FLOW AFTER ADD ACCOUNT
==================================================

Example:

User opens KrisiVeda
↓
Skips authentication
↓
Website opens
↓
Top-right shows Add Account
↓
User clicks Add Account
↓
Existing Authentication window opens
↓
User logs in/signs up
↓
Supabase session created
↓
Real user is detected
↓
Add Account disappears
↓
Real profile appears
↓
Real user's saved data loads

This must work without refreshing the page.

==================================================
14. LOGOUT FLOW
==================================================

If the user is logged in:

Profile
↓
Logout
↓
Supabase signOut()
↓
Session becomes null
↓
Clear user-specific state/cache
↓
Remove profile
↓
Remove Logout
↓
Show Add Account

The previous user's profile and farm data must NOT remain visible.

==================================================
15. DO NOT CHANGE EXISTING UI
==================================================

Do NOT redesign:

- authentication window
- authentication background
- glass effect
- login/signup forms
- dashboard
- My Farm page
- bottom navigation
- header layout
- colors
- typography

Only fix:

1. Remove fake/example account.
2. Treat skipped authentication as genuinely logged out.
3. Show Add Account for logged-out users.
4. Open real authentication when Add Account is clicked.
5. Show real profile only after real Supabase authentication.

==================================================
FINAL EXPECTED RESULT
==================================================

If user skips authentication:

Top-right:
→ Add Account

Profile:
→ no fake profile

Logout:
→ hidden

Farm data:
→ no fake data

My Farm:
→ "Sign in to view your farm details."

If user later clicks Add Account and logs in:

Top-right:
→ real user's profile

Logout:
→ visible

Farm data:
→ load that real user's saved data from Supabase

If user logs out again:

Top-right:
→ Add Account

Real profile:
→ removed

Real farm data:
→ cleared from current application state

Fake/demo account:
→ NEVER appears.

Do not add any example account under any circumstances.
