All verified — final audit shows **zero** fake-user references in the codebase, build ✓, lint 19 warnings/0 errors. Here's the full picture:

## Where "Meera Sengupta / meera@example.com / Farmer" actually came from

**It was never in the application code.** That identity was a forged Supabase session I planted in the shared preview browser's localStorage (`user_metadata.full_name`) during earlier data-isolation testing. The app correctly rendered it as "the real session's identity" — and the residue was left in shared browser storage where you could see it. I reproduced it, confirmed the mechanism, and **purged all test residue from the browser**. On any real device with a real login, this cannot appear — but the audit below closed the remaining code-level gaps so no fallback can ever fabricate identity.

## Root-cause fixes (fallback removal, not name-swapping)

1. **Auto-assigned "Farmer" role eliminated** (§9): the profile popup and Sidebar previously defaulted the role line to "Farmer" for every authenticated user. Now the role renders **only if the user actually picked one** (stored choice); otherwise the line is absent entirely. Verified live: session with no role choice → no role line anywhere.
2. **"Name unavailable" state** (§9): if a real account has no name metadata, the popup shows the new translated "Name unavailable" state instead of inventing one. Verified live with a session lacking `user_metadata`.
3. **Neutral avatar** (§10): initials derive only from real information (auth name or user-entered name); when there are none, a neutral account icon renders — no empty circle, no fake photo.
4. Grep-audited the entire project for every pattern in §6 (`demoUser`, `guestUser`, `mockUser`, `fakeUser`, `fallbackUser`, `user || {...}`, all listed names/emails): **0 matches**. The only remaining "Meera" string was a code comment, also cleaned.

## Already-correct architecture (re-verified, unchanged)

- Profile popup is **structurally unreachable** when logged out: it opens only from the avatar button, which renders only under `isAuthenticated` (real `session?.user`), and auto-closes the instant the session drops (§5/§8/§11).
- Sign out clears session → user/profile/farm state immediately; Add Account returns (§12/§14).

## All five final-behavior cases verified live

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| 1: Skip → website | Top-right **Add Account**; no profile, no logout, no fake data ✓ |
| 2: Add Account → real login | Real profile + Sign out + that user's saved data ✓ |
| 3: Logout | Session null, profile/logout gone, state cleared, Add Account back ✓ |
| 4: Refresh logged out | Add Account, no profile, no session ✓ |
| 5: Refresh logged in | Real session restored → real name, avatar, data; **no auto "Farmer" role** ✓ |

Fix a CRITICAL profile-picture data isolation bug in the KrisiVeda authentication system.

IMPORTANT:
This is a REAL multi-user authentication system using Supabase.

Each authenticated user must have their OWN completely independent profile picture.

USER A's profile picture must NEVER appear for USER B.

There must be NO shared/default/demo/fallback profile picture.

==================================================
1. CURRENT BUG
==================================================

Current behavior:

User A:
→ logs in with Gmail A
→ uploads a profile picture
→ profile picture appears correctly

Then:

User A:
→ logs out

User B:
→ logs in with a different Gmail account
→ opens profile

BUG:
→ User B sees User A's old profile picture.

This means the profile picture is currently being stored/retrieved in a shared or non-user-scoped way.

There was also a similar problem BEFORE the authentication system existed:

User uploads profile picture
→ refreshes browser
→ same picture still appears

This strongly suggests that the profile picture is being persisted somewhere such as:

- localStorage
- sessionStorage
- IndexedDB
- a global client-side state
- a fixed Supabase Storage path
- a hardcoded/default image URL
- browser cache combined with a shared storage path

Find the actual root cause.

==================================================
2. ABSOLUTE REQUIREMENT
==================================================

Profile pictures MUST be user-specific.

The only valid relationship is:

Supabase authenticated user
        ↓
user.id
        ↓
that user's profile record
        ↓
that user's profile picture

Never:

browser
        ↓
global profile picture

Never:

localStorage
        ↓
one shared profile picture

Never:

fixed storage filename
        ↓
all users

==================================================
3. USE SUPABASE USER ID
==================================================

The authenticated Supabase user's unique ID must be used to identify the profile picture.

For example, conceptually:

currentUser.id

must determine which profile image belongs to the user.

Do NOT identify a profile picture by:

- name
- email
- browser
- device
- localStorage key shared by everyone
- hardcoded filename
- "profile.jpg"
- "avatar.jpg"
- "user-profile.png"

The user's unique Supabase ID must be part of the storage/data ownership strategy.

==================================================
4. SUPABASE STORAGE PATH
==================================================

Inspect the current profile-picture upload implementation.

If the image is stored in Supabase Storage, make sure each user's image is stored in a unique user-scoped path.

For example, conceptually:

avatars/{user_id}/profile.{extension}

or:

avatars/{user_id}/{unique-file-name}.{extension}

The exact implementation should follow the project's existing Supabase Storage architecture.

DO NOT use a shared path such as:

avatars/profile.jpg

or:

avatars/avatar.png

or:

profile-images/user.jpg

if all users overwrite/read the same file.

==================================================
5. STORAGE BUCKET
==================================================

Inspect the existing Supabase Storage bucket being used for profile images.

Do not blindly create another bucket if an existing appropriate bucket already exists.

Verify:

- bucket name
- upload path
- public/private status
- Storage policies
- read policy
- upload policy
- update policy
- delete policy

The final system must ensure:

User A can access User A's profile picture.

User B must NOT be able to access User A's private profile picture through the application.

==================================================

avatar_url
profile_image
profile_picture
avatar
photo_url

auth.users.id

Context

## Root cause

The app has **no Supabase Storage bucket and no avatar column anywhere** — the picture never leaves the browser. The bug was exactly where suspected: `Header.jsx` stored the base64 image (plus name/role) under the **global** localStorage keys `krisiveda.profileImage` / `krisiveda.profileName` / `krisiveda.profileRole`, and the in-memory state never reset when the session changed. So B inherited A's photo from both storage and React state. A repo-wide grep found three more components reading those same global keys (`Sidebar.jsx`, `Dashboard.jsx`, `Settings.jsx`) — all fixed.

## The fix — ownership model: `user.id → user's own keys`

- **`src/lib/profileStore.js` (new)** — the only module that addresses profile data. Key builders `krisiveda.profileImage.<userId>` etc., plus one-time legacy migration. **The legacy global image is deliberately never adopted** — migrating it into whoever signs in next would re-create the bug once; it's deleted instead (name/role are adopted, they're not sensitive).
- **`Header.jsx`** — state now starts empty and is loaded **per identity** in a `useEffect` keyed on `user.id`: signed out → hard-clear memory (neutral `<User>` icon renders); new user → load *only* that user's scoped keys. Uploads/edit writes go through scoped keys; a null user can never upload (spec §14).
- **`useAuth.jsx`** — legacy migration runs inside `getSession` and `onAuthStateChange` (SIGNED_IN/INITIAL_SESSION/TOKEN_REFRESHED) *before* the session is published, so no consumer can render with a new identity while stale keys exist; SIGNED_OUT drops the shared legacy keys.
- **Design decision**: each account's own scoped keys **survive sign-out** — with no server-side copy they're the user's only persistence, so deleting them would destroy the picture and break "login A again → image returns". They can only ever be read back by the same `user.id`.

## Verification — all 5 scenarios passed live (real UI clicks, pixel-checked)

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| A uploads red PNG → refresh | ✓ persists, own key only |
| A signs out | ✓ modal closed, avatar cleared, memory clean |
| B logs in | ✓ "Bob Sen" + initials, **A's photo absent**, A's key untouched |

/** Bottom-nav sections in bar order (stable ids = route prefixes). */
export const SECTION_ROUTES = [
  '/',
  '/farm',
  '/ai-doctor',
  '/improve',
  '/insights',
];

/** Longest-prefix match so /ai-doctor wins over / before / is tested. */
export function resolveActiveSection(pathname) {
  if (!pathname) return null;
  return SECTION_ROUTES.find((r) =>
    r === '/' ? pathname === '/' : pathname.startsWith(r),
  ) || null;
}

/**
 * Tool routes with no nav entry of their own → their parent SECTION.
 * Derived from real in-app flows: My Farm → Crops → CropDetails offers
 * Disease/Fertilizer/Market, and the Dashboard MarketCard opens Market.
 * "/finance" is listed for future-proofing; on mobile today it is only
 * reachable from the drawer (its drawer link stays active there).
 */
const TOOL_TO_SECTION = {
  '/crops': '/farm',
  '/disease': '/farm',
  '/fertilizer': '/farm',
  '/finance': '/farm',
  '/market': '/farm',
};

/**
 * Resolve the path's own section, or its parent section for mapped tool
 * routes. Unknown paths (settings, login, …) → null = NO bottom-nav item
 * is active, which is the honest state for a page outside every section.
 */
export function resolveSectionForPath(pathname) {
  const own = resolveActiveSection(pathname);
  if (own) return own;
  const tool = Object.keys(TOOL_TO_SECTION).find((t) => pathname?.startsWith(t));
  return tool ? TOOL_TO_SECTION[tool] : null;
}

## Root cause

The bottom nav used **NavLink's built-in `isActive`**, which only highlights a link whose own route prefix matches the URL. It failed in two ways:

1. **Nested/tool routes matched nothing**: `/crops`, `/crops/parcel-0`, `/disease`, `/fertilizer`, `/finance`, `/market` have no nav entry — so *no* item went green (the "none highlighted" case).
2. **Prefix collisions matched the wrong item**: `/crops` starts with both `/` and `/farm`, and neither NavLink is `end` — so on a Crops/parcel page **two** items claimed active (the "wrong item" case). Transitions, language and theme were red herrings — the URL never changes during them; the mismatch was purely path→section resolution.

## The fix (single source of truth, zero redesign)

- **`src/lib/activeSection.js` (new)** — one resolver: current route → main section. The five stable section routes (`/`, `/farm`, `/ai-doctor`, `/improve`, `/insights`) with longest-prefix matching, plus a tool-route map derived from the app's real flows (`/crops` + the CropDetails tools → **My Farm**). Stable route prefixes are the identifiers — never translated labels.
- **`MobileNavigation.jsx`** — active class now comes from `resolveSectionForPath(location.pathname)`; NavLink still handles navigation, but per-link `isActive` no longer decides the highlight. No stored state, no click-order memory — the URL decides, so refresh/direct-nav/back-forward all work by construction.
- **`MobilePageTransition.jsx`** — upgraded the rapid-tap guard from "drop the tap" to **last-tap-wins**: a tap during a transition is held and queued, then flushed on lock release (with a stale-queue guard). Rapid Overview→…→Insights now ends on Insights, the tab the user aimed for.
- **`MobileDrawer.jsx` + `Sidebar.jsx`** — same resolver, so the drawer and desktop sidebar agree with the bottom bar (e.g. `/market` keeps বাজার তথ্য highlighted).

## Verified live (mobile viewport, real UI interactions)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| 5 main sections via real taps, exactly 1 green each | ✓ all |
| Refresh + direct load (`/farm`, `/disease`) | ✓ correct item |
| Nested detail `/crops/parcel-0` + cold deep-link | ✓ My Farm stays green |
| Back button from detail | ✓ consistent |
| Rapid taps ×2 rounds | ✓ last tap wins, never 0/2 active |
| Bengali + light theme | ✓ same item, `--active` color intact |
| Sign-out → re-login | ✓ nav resets cleanly, no stale highlight |

**Design notes**: on `/settings` (a page outside every section) no bottom-nav item is active — that's the honest state, not a bug. "Improve Yield" is the en label for `/improve`; the screenshot's wording came from the same nav data. Build ✓, lint **18w/0e** (one below baseline), all test residue purged. Files changed: 4 edited, 1 added — no design, CSS, or route changes.

Worth exploring next: giving tool pages their own bottom-nav presence now that section resolution is centralized, adding a route-level regression test for the resolver, or returning to the profile/avatar server-side persistence milestone.

-- migration_avatar.sql — server-side profile picture (cross-device sync).
--
-- RUN ORDER: apply migration_onboarding.sql FIRST (this file needs the
-- profiles table). Then run THIS file once in the Supabase SQL Editor.
-- Safe to re-run: IF NOT EXISTS / drop+create policies throughout.
--
-- Architecture (profile spec §3–§6):
--   upload → Storage bucket "avatars", object path "<user_id>/avatar.<ext>"
--          → profiles.avatar_url stores that path
--          → any device loads profiles.avatar_url for the same user.id
--            and renders the public URL (unique per user + cache-safe).
--
-- OWNERSHIP (spec §4/§11): every object lives under a folder named by the
-- uploader's auth.uid(); policies enforce that only the owner can write
-- their folder and only authenticated users can read. No shared path.
-- ============================================================================

-- 1) avatar_url on the existing profile row (no second profile system).
alter table public.profiles
    add column if not exists avatar_url text not null default '';

-- 2) Storage bucket: public read (avatars are rendered as <img src>),
--    write strictly through the owner-scoped policies below.
insert into storage.buckets (id, name, public)
values ('avatars', 'avatars', true)
on conflict (id) do update set public = true;

-- 3) Policies — user-scoped paths ONLY ("<uid>/avatar.*").
--    READ: any authenticated user may fetch avatar objects. Objects are
--    addressed per-owner, so user B can only reach A's picture by
--    already knowing A's exact public URL (same trust level as the
--    profiles row itself; the app never exposes other users' URLs).
drop policy if exists "avatars_read_authenticated" on storage.objects;
create policy "avatars_read_authenticated"
    on storage.objects for select
    to authenticated
    using (bucket_id = 'avatars');

--    WRITE/UPDATE/DELETE: the first path segment MUST be the caller's
--    own auth.uid() — one user can never create, replace or remove
--    another user's picture.
drop policy if exists "avatars_insert_own" on storage.objects;
create policy "avatars_insert_own"
    on storage.objects for insert
    to authenticated
    with check (
        bucket_id = 'avatars'
        and (storage.foldername(name))[1] = auth.uid()::text
    );

drop policy if exists "avatars_update_own" on storage.objects;
create policy "avatars_update_own"
    on storage.objects for update
    to authenticated
    using (
        bucket_id = 'avatars'
        and (storage.foldername(name))[1] = auth.uid()::text
    )
    with check (
        bucket_id = 'avatars'
        and (storage.foldername(name))[1] = auth.uid()::text
    );

drop policy if exists "avatars_delete_own" on storage.objects;
create policy "avatars_delete_own"
    on storage.objects for delete
    to authenticated
    using (
        bucket_id = 'avatars'
        and (storage.foldername(name))[1] = auth.uid()::text
    );

-- 4) Expose the cache-safe public URL without duplicating logic in the
--    client: the stored avatar_url is the object path; this generated
--    column turns it into the fetchable URL on read.
create or replace function public.avatar_public_url(path text)
returns text
language sql
immutable
as $$
    select case
        when path is null or path = '' then null
        else 'https://' || split_part(current_setting('request.headers', true)::json->>'host', ':', 1)
             || '/storage/v1/object/public/avatars/' || path
    end;
$$;

-- NOTE: the function above is only a convenience helper; the client
-- (profileService.js) builds the URL with supabase.storage.getPublicUrl,
-- which knows the project host. The column stays a plain path.

{"kind":"tool","id":"5oXNH43zvLk","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"src/lib/profileService.js","instructions":"Add the server avatar service: fetch path, public URL builder, user-scoped upload, profile-row save, and image downscale helper","content":"/**
 * profileService.js — SERVER-side profile picture (cross-device sync).
 *
 * Pure Supabase logic layer (same pattern as onboardingService.js): no
 * React, no UI. The BROWSER is no longer the source of truth:
 *
 *   upload → Storage bucket "avatars" at "<user_id>/avatar-<ts>.<ext>"
 *          → profiles.avatar_url stores that object path
 *          → any device: fetch profiles.avatar_url for the same user.id
 *            → supabase.storage.getPublicUrl → same picture everywhere
 *
 * GRACEFUL DEGRADATION (project-wide pattern): until migration_avatar.sql
 * is applied (profiles.avatar_url column + avatars bucket), every call
 * fails softly — the app keeps working on the user-scoped localStorage
 * copy. No raw database error ever reaches a farmer.
 */

import { supabase } from "./supabaseClient";

const BUCKET = "avatars";
/** Longest edge of the re-encoded copy kept in localStorage. The FULL
 *  original always goes to Supabase; the small copy is only an offline/
 *  instant-paint cache. */
export const AVATAR_CACHE_EDGE = 512;

function warn(context, error) {
    if (import.meta.env.DEV) {
        // eslint-disable-next-line no-console
        console.warn(`[profile] ${context}:`, error?.message || error);
    }
}

function isSchemaError(error) {
    if (!error) return false;
    const msg = String(error.message || error).toLowerCase();
    return (
        msg.includes("could not find the table") ||
        msg.includes("column") ||
        msg.includes("schema cache") ||
        msg.includes("does not exist") ||
        msg.includes("bucket not found") ||
        msg.includes("permission") ||
        msg.includes("jwt") ||
        msg.includes("row-level security")
    );
}

/** Read the stored avatar PATH for a user ('' when none/unavailable). */
export async function fetchAvatarPath(userId) {
    if (!userId || !supabase) return "";
    try {
        const { data, error } = await supabase
            .from("profiles")
            .select("avatar_url")
            .eq("id", userId)
            .maybeSingle();
        if (error) {
            if (!isSchemaError(error)) warn("avatar fetch failed", error);
            else warn("avatar fetch — migration not applied", error);
            return "";
        }
        return typeof data?.avatar_url === "string" ? data.avatar_url : "";
    } catch (err) {
        warn("avatar fetch threw", err);
        return "";
    }
}

/** Public URL for a storage path ('' when the path is empty/unknown). */
export function getAvatarPublicUrl(path) {
    if (!path || !supabase) return "";
    try {
        const { data } = supabase.storage.from(BUCKET).getPublicUrl(path);
        return data?.publicUrl || "";
    } catch {
        return "";
    }
}

/**
 * Load the user's avatar URL from the SERVER (the cross-device path):
 * profiles.avatar_url → public Storage URL. Returns '' when the user has
 * no uploaded picture or the migration/bucket is not available yet.
 */
export async function fetchServerAvatarUrl(userId) {
    const path = await fetchAvatarPath(userId);
    return getAvatarPublicUrl(path);
}

/**
 * Upload a picked image for the CURRENT user and record it on their
 * profile row. Path is user-scoped ("<uid>/avatar-<ts>.<ext>") — no
 * shared filename, enforced again by the bucket's RLS policies.
 * Returns the storage path, or null on any failure (caller keeps the
 * local copy and may show an error).
 */
export async function uploadAvatar(userId, file) {
    if (!userId || !supabase || !file) return null;
    const ext =
        file.type === "image/png"
            ? "png"
            : file.type === "image/webp"
              ? "webp"
              : "jpg";
    // Unique name per upload → browsers never serve a stale cached
    // avatar after replacement, and old objects remain for rollback.
    const path = `${userId}/avatar-${Date.now()}.${ext}`;
    try {
        const { error } = await supabase.storage
            .from(BUCKET)
            .upload(path, file, {
                contentType: file.type || "image/jpeg",
                cacheControl: "31536000", // unique name → immutable object
                upsert: false,
            });
        if (error) {
            if (!isSchemaError(error)) warn("avatar upload failed", error);
            else warn("avatar upload — migration not applied", error);
            return null;
        }
        const saved = await saveAvatarPath(userId, path);
        if (!saved) {
            // Object stored but row write failed: the picture is on the
            // server; a retry will re-save. Report partial success as
            // failure so the caller keeps the local cache.
            return null;
        }
        return path;
    } catch (err) {
        warn("avatar upload threw", err);
        return null;
    }
}

/** Persist the avatar path on the user's profile row (no-op when absent). */
export async function saveAvatarPath(userId, path) {
    if (!userId || !supabase) return false;
    try {
        const { error } = await supabase
            .from("profiles")
            .upsert(
                { id: userId, avatar_url: path, updated_at: new Date().toISOString() },
                { onConflict: "id" },
            );
        if (error) {
            if (!isSchemaError(error)) warn("avatar save failed", error);
            else warn("avatar save — migration not applied", error);
            return false;
        }
        return true;
    } catch (err) {
        warn("avatar save threw", err);
        return false;
    }
}

/**
 * Re-encode a picked image to a ≤512px JPEG/PNG data URL for the instant
 * local cache. Resolves to the data URL, or rejects if the browser
 * cannot decode it (caller falls back to the raw FileReader data URL).
 */
export function downscaleToDataUrl(file) {
    return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
        const url = URL.createObjectURL(file);
        const img = new Image();
        img.onload = () => {
            try {
                const scale = Math.min(
                    1,
                    AVATAR_CACHE_EDGE / Math.max(img.width, img.height),
                );
                const canvas = document.createElement("canvas");
                canvas.width = Math.max(1, Math.round(img.width * scale));
                canvas.height = Math.max(1, Math.round(img.height * scale));
                canvas.getContext("2d").drawImage(img, 0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height);
                URL.revokeObjectURL(url);
                // PNG keeps transparency; everything else → compact JPEG.
                resolve(canvas.toDataURL(file.type === "image/png" ? "image/png" : "image/jpeg", 0.85));
            } catch (e) {
                URL.revokeObjectURL(url);
                reject(e);
            }
        };
        img.onerror = () => {
            URL.revokeObjectURL(url);
            reject(new Error("decode failed"));
        };
        img.src = url;
    });
}

## 1. Root cause

**The profile picture never left the browser.** A full audit found: zero Supabase Storage code (no `.storage.` call anywhere), no bucket, no `avatar_url` column (the unapplied `migration_onboarding.sql` defines `profiles` without one), and no upload path. The image existed **only** as a base64 data URL in `localStorage` under `krisiveda.profileImage.<userId>`. My previous fix made that key *user-scoped* — correct for cross-**user** isolation, but still device-local by nature. Same account, second device → empty localStorage → no picture. React Context only mirrored what localStorage had; nothing else was involved (no sessionStorage, IndexedDB, Zustand/Redux, or React Query, and no fallback image).

## 2. Files changed

- **`supabase/migration_avatar.sql` (new)** — `avatar_url` column on `profiles`; `avatars` storage bucket (public read); RLS storage policies: any authenticated user may read, but **insert/update/delete require the object's first path segment to equal `auth.uid()`** — no user can write or overwrite another's picture, no shared path possible.
- **`src/lib/profileService.js` (new)** — pure Supabase layer: `uploadAvatar` (Storage upload + `profiles.avatar_url` write), `fetchServerAvatarUrl` (path → `getPublicUrl`), plus `downscaleToDataUrl`. Follows the project's graceful-degradation pattern.
- **`src/components/layout/Header.jsx`** — on sign-in, loads the **server** avatar (overrides the local cache when present); on upload: instant memory paint → small re-encoded ≤512px cache in localStorage → **original file to Storage** → path saved to `profiles.avatar_url` → cache updated to the server URL. Full-size base64 never touches localStorage (quota safety).

## 3–4. Table, bucket, path structure

- Table: `public.profiles` (existing row, new `avatar_url` column — no second profile system)
- Bucket: `avatars` — path **`<user_id>/avatar-<timestamp>.<ext>`** (user-scoped, unique per upload → cache-safe replacement)

## 5. How cross-device sync works now

Upload: file → Storage under the user's folder → path into the user's profile row. Any device logging into that account reads `profiles.avatar_url` for its own `user.id` and renders the same public URL. localStorage is now only a cache/optimization — never the authority.

+--          → profiles.avatar_url stores that path

+-- ============================================================================

+--    write strictly through the owner-scoped policies below.
+insert into storage.buckets (id, name, public)
+values ('avatars', 'avatars', true)
+on conflict (id) do update set public = true;
+
+-- 3) Policies — user-scoped paths ONLY ("<uid>/avatar.*").
+--    READ: any authenticated user may fetch avatar objects. Objects are
+--    addressed per-owner, so user B can only reach A's picture by
+--    already knowing A's exact public URL (same trust level as the
+--    profiles row itself; the app never exposes other users' URLs).
+drop policy if exists "avatars_read_authenticated" on storage.objects;
+create policy "avatars_read_authenticated"
+    on storage.objects for select
+    to authenticated
+    using (bucket_id = 'avatars');

+create policy "avatars_insert_own"
+    on storage.objects for insert

 * Tool routes with no nav entry of their own → their parent SECTION.
 * Derived from real in-app flows: My Farm → Crops → CropDetails offers
 * Disease/Fertilizer/Market, and the Dashboard MarketCard opens Market.
 * "/finance" is listed for future-proofing; on mobile today it is only
 * reachable from the drawer (its drawer link stays active there).
 */
const TOOL_TO_SECTION = {
  '/crops': '/farm',
  '/disease': '/farm',
  '/fertilizer': '/farm',
  '/finance': '/farm',
  '/market': '/farm',
};

/**
 * Resolve the path's own section, or its parent section for mapped tool
 * routes. Unknown paths (settings, login, …) → null = NO bottom-nav item
 * is active, which is the honest state for a page outside every section.
 */
export function resolveSectionForPath(pathname) {
  const own = resolveActiveSection(pathname);
  if (own) return own;
  const tool = Object.keys(TOOL_TO_SECTION).find((t) => pathname?.startsWith(t));
  return tool ? TOOL_TO_SECTION[tool] : null;
}","newString":"/**
 * Resolve the path's own section, or null for pages outside every
 * bottom-nav section. Sidebar-only features (Rice Varieties /crops,
 * Disease /disease, Fertilizer /fertilizer, Cost & Profit /finance,
 * Market Intelligence /market, Settings /settings) are STANDALONE —
 * they activate NOTHING (spec: "activeItem = null" is a valid state;
 * no fallback may keep My Farm green just because the shell contains
 * them). The single exception is a GENUINE child of a bottom-nav
 * section: a My Farm parcel detail (/crops/parcel-*) — My Farm stays
 * active there because that page IS part of the My Farm flow.
 */
export function resolveSectionForPath(pathname) {
  if (!pathname) return null;
  const own = resolveActiveSection(pathname);
  if (own) return own;
  // Genuine child of My Farm: the parcel detail opened from the farm map.
  if (/^\/crops\/parcel-/.test(pathname)) return '/farm';
  return null;
}","allowMultiple":false},{"oldString":" * Why this exists: React Router's NavLink isActive is per-link and can

## Root cause

The bug lived in `src/lib/activeSection.js` — the route→section resolver introduced with the earlier active-state fix. Its `TOOL_TO_SECTION` map deliberately routed the sidebar-feature paths (`/crops`, `/disease`, `/fertilizer`, `/finance`, `/market`) to `/farm`, so **My Farm stayed green on every sidebar feature** by design of that map. Your navigation policy has changed (those features are standalone, `activeItem = null` is a valid state), so the map had to go. No CSS tricks, no new state — the underlying logic changed at the single source of truth, which all three navs share.

## What changed

- **`src/lib/activeSection.js`** — removed the tool→section fallback entirely. Now: the five section routes match themselves; the *only* non-section path that keeps a highlight is a genuine My Farm child — the parcel detail `/crops/parcel-*` (opened from the farm map, not the sidebar). Everything else — `/crops` (Rice Varieties), `/disease`, `/fertilizer`, `/finance`, `/market`, `/settings` — resolves to `null` → **no bottom-nav item is active**.
- **`MobileNavigation.jsx` / `MobileDrawer.jsx`** — comment updates only (no logic change); sidebar untouched.
- Linter nit: replaced a regex test with `pathname.startsWith('/crops/parcel-')`.

Implement client-side profile-image compression for the existing Krisiveda profile-picture upload system.

IMPORTANT:
Do NOT redesign the profile UI.
Do NOT change the existing Supabase authentication system.
Do NOT change the existing avatar bucket architecture.
Do NOT create another profile-image system.

CURRENT STORAGE ARCHITECTURE:

Supabase Storage bucket:
avatars

Profile image path:
<user_id>/avatar.<ext>

Database:
profiles.avatar_url

The existing cross-device synchronization must remain unchanged.

==================================================
GOAL
==================================================

When the user selects a profile image:

Original image
→ validate
→ compress in the browser
→ upload ONLY the compressed image to Supabase Storage
→ save the resulting storage path in profiles.avatar_url
→ display the compressed image

The original large image must NOT be uploaded to Supabase.

==================================================
MAXIMUM INPUT FILE SIZE
==================================================

Allow the user to select an image up to:

20 MB

If the original file is larger than 20 MB:

- reject the file
- do NOT start compression
- do NOT upload it
- show a clear existing-style validation message
- keep the current profile picture unchanged

The 20 MB limit applies to the ORIGINAL selected file.

Do not silently accept files larger than 20 MB.

==================================================
SUPPORTED IMAGE TYPES
==================================================

Accept normal image formats supported by the existing profile uploader, such as:

JPEG
JPG
PNG
WEBP

If the current application already has a specific allowed image-type list, preserve it.

Do not accept arbitrary non-image files.

==================================================
COMPRESSION
==================================================

Implement browser-side image compression before Supabase upload.

Prefer a lightweight dependency only if the project already has a suitable image-compression library.

Otherwise use the browser Canvas API / HTMLCanvasElement.toBlob() so no unnecessary dependency is introduced.

Do NOT use base64/data URLs as the storage format.

Use Blob/File output.

==================================================
IMAGE QUALITY
==================================================

The goal is:

small file size
+
good visual quality
+
no obvious degradation

Do NOT aggressively destroy image quality.

Use adaptive compression.

For example:

- Start with high JPEG/WebP quality.
- Check the resulting compressed file size.
- If it is still too large, gradually reduce quality.
- Continue until the target size is reached or a safe minimum quality is reached.

Do NOT blindly compress every image to extremely low quality.

==================================================
OUTPUT TARGET
==================================================

Aim for a compressed output around:

2–5 MB maximum when practical.

However:

DO NOT force every image to exactly 2 MB.

If a high-resolution image can remain visually excellent at a larger size while still staying reasonably small, preserve quality.

The final goal is efficient storage and fast loading, not maximum compression at any cost.

==================================================
DIMENSIONS
==================================================

Profile pictures do not need enormous dimensions.

Before compression, inspect the image dimensions.

If the image is extremely large, resize it proportionally while preserving its aspect ratio.

Do NOT stretch or distort the image.

Do NOT crop the user's image automatically.

Do NOT change the visible composition.

Use a reasonable maximum dimension for a profile picture, such as 1600px on the longest side.

If the original image is already smaller than the maximum dimension, do not upscale it.

==================================================
FORMAT
==================================================

For photographs:

Prefer JPEG or WebP output if supported by the existing application.

For images where transparency is important:

preserve PNG/WebP transparency when necessary.

Do not blindly convert every image to JPEG if doing so would destroy transparency.

The uploaded file extension and contentType must match the actual compressed output format.

==================================================
EXIF / ORIENTATION
==================================================

Handle mobile photos correctly.

Some phone photos contain EXIF orientation metadata.

Make sure the compressed image is rendered with the correct orientation.

The user must NOT see a sideways/upside-down profile picture after compression.

==================================================
UPLOAD FLOW
==================================================

The final upload flow must be:

User selects file
↓
Validate file type
↓
Validate original size <= 20 MB
↓
Read image
↓
Correct orientation
↓
Resize only if necessary
↓
Compress
↓
Create final File/Blob
↓
Upload compressed file to:
avatars/<user_id>/avatar.<ext>
↓
Update profiles.avatar_url
↓
Refresh/reload the profile image
↓
Clean temporary browser resources

Do NOT upload the original file at any point.

==================================================
USER EXPERIENCE
==================================================

While compression/upload is happening:

Show the existing loading/progress state if one already exists.

If no suitable state exists, add a minimal existing-style loading state.

Do not freeze the UI.

Prevent duplicate uploads while the current operation is running.

If compression fails:

- show a clear error
- do not upload the original file
- keep the previous avatar unchanged

If Supabase upload fails:

- show the existing upload error UI
- keep the previous avatar unchanged
- do not overwrite profiles.avatar_url with an invalid path

==================================================
PROFILE IMAGE REPLACEMENT
==================================================

Preserve the existing user-specific storage architecture.

Do not change it to a shared path.

The path must remain associated with the authenticated user's ID.

Make sure User A cannot upload into User B's folder.

Make sure User B cannot overwrite User A's profile image.

==================================================
CACHE / STALE IMAGE
==================================================

Be careful with browser/CDN caching when replacing an avatar.

If the current implementation uses:

<user_id>/avatar.jpg

and overwrites the same path, avoid a stale old image being displayed after a successful upload.

Prefer a unique filename/versioned path when appropriate, for example:

<user_id>/avatar-<unique-id>.jpg

Then update profiles.avatar_url to the new path.

If you change the path strategy, also safely remove the previous avatar owned by the same user if the existing implementation supports cleanup.

Do NOT delete another user's files.

Supabase documentation notes that uploading to a new path can avoid CDN propagation/stale-content issues compared with overwriting the same path.

==================================================
DATABASE
==================================================

Do NOT create another avatar column.

Continue using:

profiles.avatar_url

Store the Storage object path, not a browser-local object URL.

Do NOT store:

blob:http://...
data:image/...
base64 image data

inside profiles.avatar_url.

The database must contain the Supabase Storage object path.

==================================================
CROSS-DEVICE REQUIREMENT
==================================================

After compression is implemented, this MUST still work:

PC:
Login Account A
→ select 15 MB photo
→ browser compresses it
→ upload compressed file
→ profiles.avatar_url updated

Mobile:
Login Account A
→ fetch profiles.avatar_url
→ same compressed profile image appears

Another browser:
Login Account A
→ same image appears

The browser's localStorage/sessionStorage must NOT be the source of truth.

Supabase remains the source of truth.

==================================================
IMPORTANT TEST CASES
==================================================

Test:

1. 500 KB image
→ should upload normally with appropriate optimization.

2. 5 MB image
→ should compress if beneficial.

3. 15 MB image
→ should compress before upload.

4. 19.9 MB image
→ should be accepted and compressed before upload.

5. 20 MB image
→ should be accepted if it is within the defined byte limit.

→ reject before compression/upload.

7. Very high-resolution phone photo
→ resize proportionally and compress.

8. Portrait phone photo
→ orientation must remain correct.

9. PNG with transparency
→ do not destroy transparency unnecessarily.

10. Upload failure
→ previous avatar remains.

11. Compression failure
→ previous avatar remains.

12. User A upload
→ User B must never receive User A's avatar.

13. PC upload
→ mobile same account must show the same avatar.

==================================================
SUPABASE BUCKET CONFIGURATION
==================================================

Do NOT change the existing avatar bucket security policies unless absolutely required.

The application already has:

avatars bucket
+
user-scoped Storage policies
+
profiles.avatar_url

Preserve them.

If the bucket's current 50 MB limit is still present, keep the application-level original-input limit at 20 MB.

The important rule is:

20 MB = maximum original file selected by the user.

Compression happens BEFORE upload.

==================================================
FINAL REQUIREMENT
==================================================

The final architecture must be:

Original image
(max 20 MB)
        ↓
Browser validation
        ↓
Browser compression/resizing
        ↓
Compressed image
(preferably ~2–5 MB when practical)
        ↓
Supabase Storage
avatars/<user_id>/...
        ↓
profiles.avatar_url
        ↓
Any device
        ↓
Same profile image

Do not redesign anything.
Do not add demo users.
Do not add fake avatars.

// Edge Function: delete-account  (v2 — self-diagnosing runtime errors)
//
// Permanently deletes the AUTHENTICATED caller's account. Deploy:
//   Dashboard → Edge Functions → delete-account → paste this file → Deploy
//   (or: npx supabase functions deploy delete-account --project-ref <ref>)

// SECURITY MODEL (unchanged):
//   • Identity comes EXCLUSIVELY from the verified Authorization bearer
//     JWT (admin.auth.getUser). No user_id is accepted from the client,
//     so a caller can only ever delete THEMSELVES.
//   • The service-role key is read only from server env (auto-injected
//     by the platform for deployed functions) and NEVER appears in a
//     response, log, or the frontend bundle.
//
// v2 CHANGES (runtime-500 debugging, per incident triage):
//   1. deleteUser now passes { should_soft_delete: false } EXPLICITLY —
//      GoTrue may otherwise soft-delete (deleted_at) instead of removing
//      the user, which changed what the confirmation step saw.
//   2. The confirmation step treats BOTH a missing user AND a user
//      carrying deleted_at/soft_deleted_at as confirmed deletion; only a
//      fully intact user is a failure.
//   3. Every operation logs its own failure via console.error as
//      structured JSON {op, message} — NO tokens, keys, or user PII.
//   4. Error RESPONSES now carry op + detail so the exact failing
//      operation is visible in the browser Network tab (values are
//      GoTrue/PostgREST error strings only — never secrets).
//   5. Cascade verification: before deleting, the function reads the
//      caller's profiles/farms row counts (service role bypasses RLS);
//      after deletion it re-checks that the profiles row is gone —
//      proving the auth.users FK cascade actually fired.
// ============================================================================

import { createClient } from "jsr:@supabase/supabase-js@2";

const CORS_HEADERS = {
    "Access-Control-Allow-Origin": "*",
    "Access-Control-Allow-Headers":
        "authorization, x-client-info, apikey, content-type",
    "Access-Control-Allow-Methods": "POST, OPTIONS",
};

function json(body, status = 200) {
    return new Response(JSON.stringify(body), {
        status,
        headers: { ...CORS_HEADERS, "Content-Type": "application/json" },
    });
}

/** Uniform error shape — safe detail only (error strings, never secrets). */
function fail(status, code, message, op, detail) {
    return json(
        { success: false, error: { code, message, op, detail: detail ?? null } },
        status,
    );
}

/** Safe structured server log: op + message only. Never tokens/keys/PII. */
function logError(op, err) {
    const message = err?.message ? String(err.message) : String(err ?? "unknown");
    console.error(JSON.stringify({ event: "delete_account_error", op, message }));
}

Deno.serve(async (req) => {
    // Preflight: 200 + CORS headers. Echo the browser's requested header
    // list back verbatim, so the preflight can never fail on an
    // incomplete Access-Control-Allow-Headers list.
    if (req.method === "OPTIONS") {
        return new Response("ok", {
            status: 200,
            headers: {
                ...CORS_HEADERS,
                "Access-Control-Allow-Headers":
                    req.headers.get("Access-Control-Request-Headers") ??
                    CORS_HEADERS["Access-Control-Allow-Headers"],
            },
        });
    }
    if (req.method !== "POST") {
        return fail(405, "method_not_allowed", "Use POST.", "method_check");
    }

    const serviceKey = Deno.env.get("SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY") ?? "";
    if (!serviceKey) {
        // Mis-configured deployment — refuse loudly, delete nothing.
        console.error(
            JSON.stringify({ event: "delete_account_error", op: "env_check", message: "SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY not set" }),
        );
        return fail(500, "server_misconfigured", "Service is not configured.", "env_check");
    }
    // Availability logged as a boolean only — never the value.
    console.log(JSON.stringify({ event: "delete_account_start", has_service_key: true }));

    const admin = createClient(
        Deno.env.get("SUPABASE_URL") ?? "",
        serviceKey,
        { auth: { autoRefreshToken: false, persistSession: false } },
    );

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    // 1) IDENTITY — verified from the bearer JWT only.
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------
    const authHeader = req.headers.get("Authorization") ?? "";
    if (!authHeader.toLowerCase().startsWith("bearer ")) {
        return fail(401, "no_credentials", "Missing bearer token.", "auth_header");
    }
    const token = authHeader.slice(7).trim();
    let callerId = "";
    try {
        const { data, error } = await admin.auth.getUser(token);
        if (error || !data?.user?.id) {
            logError("jwt_verify", error ?? "no user in token");
            return fail(401, "invalid_token", "Invalid or expired session.", "jwt_verify");
        }
        callerId = data.user.id;
    } catch (err) {
        logError("jwt_verify", err);
        return fail(401, "invalid_token", "Invalid or expired session.", "jwt_verify");
    }

    try {
        // --------------------------------------------------------------
        // 2) PRE-DELETE STATE — read-only diagnostics (RLS bypassed via
        //    service role). Proves which migrations are applied and how
        //    much user-owned data the cascade must remove.
        // --------------------------------------------------------------
        let profilesRow = "unknown";
        let farmsRow = "unknown";
        try {
            const { data: p, error: pe } = await admin
                .from("profiles")
                .select("id")
                .eq("id", callerId)
                .maybeSingle();
            profilesRow = pe
                ? `unavailable: ${pe.message}`
                : p
                  ? "present"
                  : "absent";
        } catch (err) {
            logError("precheck_profiles", err);
        }
        try {
            const { data: f, error: fe } = await admin
                .from("farms")
                .select("id")
                .eq("user_id", callerId)
                .maybeSingle();
            farmsRow = fe ? `unavailable: ${fe.message}` : f ? "present" : "absent";
        } catch (err) {
            logError("precheck_farms", err);
        }
        console.log(
            JSON.stringify({
                event: "delete_account_precheck",
                user_id: callerId,
                profiles_row: profilesRow,
                farms_row: farmsRow,
            }),
        );

        // --------------------------------------------------------------
        // 3) AVATAR FILES — delete EVERY object in the caller's own
        //    folder (versioned names → possibly several). Storage API
        //    only; the prefix is built from the verified id, so no other
        //    user's folder is addressable.
        // --------------------------------------------------------------
        let avatarsDeleted = 0;
        try {
            const objects: string[] = [];
            let offset = 0;
            for (;;) {
                const { data, error } = await admin.storage
                    .from("avatars")
                    .list(callerId, {
                        limit: 100,
                        offset,
                        sortBy: { column: "created_at", order: "desc" },
                    });
                if (error) {
                    logError("avatar_list", error);
                    break;
                }
                for (const o of data ?? []) {
                    if (o?.name) objects.push(`${callerId}/${o.name}`);
                }
                if (!data || data.length < 100) break;
                offset += 100;
            }
            if (objects.length) {
                const { error } = await admin.storage
                    .from("avatars")
                    .remove(objects);
                if (error) logError("avatar_remove", error);
                else avatarsDeleted = objects.length;
            }
        } catch (err) {
            logError("avatar_cleanup", err);
            /* Storage hiccup: continue — the account itself is the point. */
        }

        // --------------------------------------------------------------
        // 4) AUTH USER — EXPLICIT permanent deletion. FK CASCADE
        //    (auth.users.id → profiles/farms/land_parcels) removes every
        //    user-owned row; auth schema cascades remove sessions.
        // --------------------------------------------------------------
        const { error: delErr } = await admin.auth.deleteUser(callerId, {
            should_soft_delete: false,
        });
        if (delErr) {
            // PostgREST FK violations / GoTrue failures surface here —
            // the message is the actual database/auth error (no secrets).
            logError("auth_delete", delErr);
            return fail(
                500,
                "delete_failed",
                "The account could not be deleted. Nothing has been removed — please try again.",
                "auth_delete",
                String(delErr.message ?? delErr),
            );
        }

        // --------------------------------------------------------------
        // 5) HARD CONFIRMATION — never report success on trust:
        //    • user gone (error)               → confirmed (hard delete)
        //    • user present WITH deleted_at    → confirmed (soft delete)
        //    • user fully intact               → NOT confirmed → 500
        // --------------------------------------------------------------
        let confirmed = false;
        let confirmMode = "unknown";
        try {
            const { data: check, error: checkErr } = await admin.auth.getUserById(callerId);
            if (checkErr) {
                confirmed = true; // any lookup error ⇒ the user is gone
                confirmMode = "user_gone";
            } else {
                const u: Record<string, unknown> | undefined = check?.user as
                    | Record<string, unknown>
                    | undefined;
                const softDeletedAt =
                    (u?.deleted_at as string | undefined) ??
                    (u?.soft_deleted_at as string | undefined) ??
                    (u?.softDeleteAt as string | undefined) ??
                    null;
                if (softDeletedAt) {
                    confirmed = true;
                    confirmMode = `soft_deleted_at=${softDeletedAt}`;
                } else {
                    confirmed = false;
                    confirmMode = "user_still_intact";
                }
            }
        } catch (err) {
            logError("delete_confirm", err);
            confirmed = false;
            confirmMode = "confirm_lookup_threw";
        }
        if (!confirmed) {
            return fail(
                500,
                "delete_not_confirmed",
                "Deletion could not be confirmed. If you were logged out, the account is already gone; otherwise please try again.",
                "delete_confirm",
                confirmMode,
            );
        }

        // --------------------------------------------------------------
        // 6) CASCADE VERIFICATION — the profiles row must be gone after
        //    the auth user was deleted (or the table must not exist yet).
        //    Read-only; result logged for the Function Logs.
        // --------------------------------------------------------------
        let cascade = "unknown";
        try {
            const { data: p2, error: pe2 } = await admin
                .from("profiles")
                .select("id")
                .eq("id", callerId)
                .maybeSingle();
            if (pe2) cascade = `unavailable: ${pe2.message}`;
            else cascade = p2 ? "ROW_STILL_PRESENT (cascade failed!)" : "row_removed";
        } catch (err) {
            logError("cascade_check", err);
        }

        console.log(
            JSON.stringify({
                event: "account_deleted",
                user_id: callerId,
                avatars_deleted: avatarsDeleted,
                confirm_mode: confirmMode,
                cascade_check: cascade,
                at: new Date().toISOString(),
            }),
        );

        return json({
            success: true,
            data: { userId: callerId, avatarsDeleted, cascade },
        });
    } catch (err) {
        logError("unexpected", err);
        return fail(
            500,
            "unexpected",
            "Something went wrong while deleting the account. Please try again.",
            "unexpected",
            err?.message ? String(err.message) : null,
        );
    }
});

{"kind":"tool","id":"6NEvh2bfIvw","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"supabase/functions/delete-account/index.ts","instructions":"Final instrumented delete-account function: DELETE_ACCOUNT step logging, safe structured errors with step/detail, hard delete with soft-delete-aware confirmation and retry, cascade verification, preserved CORS and JWT security.","content":"// ============================================================================
// Edge Function: delete-account  (v3 — instrumented for runtime debugging)
//
// Permanently deletes the AUTHENTICATED caller's account. Deploy:
//   Dashboard → Edge Functions → delete-account → paste this file → Deploy
//   (or: npx supabase functions deploy delete-account --project-ref <ref>)
//
// WHY THIS CLIENT (verified, not guessed): "@supabase/server" is NOT a
// published module — the server-side createServerClient people find in
// searches belongs to "@supabase/ssr", a cookie-based helper for
// Next.js/Astro servers that does not run on Supabase Edge Functions.
// The CURRENT Supabase Edge Functions pattern is jsr:@supabase/
// supabase-js@2 + the platform-injected SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY,
// which is exactly what this function uses.
//
// SECURITY MODEL (unchanged, verified working — OPTIONS 200, JWT
// gateway-validated, POST reaches this code):
//   • Identity comes EXCLUSIVELY from the verified Authorization bearer
//     JWT (admin.auth.getUser re-checks it against GoTrue). No user_id
//     is accepted from the client — a caller can only delete THEMSELVES.
//   • The service-role key is read only from server env and NEVER
//     appears in logs, responses, or the frontend.
//
// v3 CHANGES (runtime-500 debugging):
//   1. Step-by-step "DELETE_ACCOUNT: …" logging so the Function Logs
//      show exactly which operation fails.
//   2. Errors are logged safely: step name + error name + message +
//      status/code. NEVER tokens, refresh tokens, keys, the raw
//      Authorization header, or user passwords.
//   3. Error RESPONSES are safe and structured:
//      { success:false, error:"delete_failed", step:"auth_delete",
//        message:"…", detail:"…" } — detail carries only the upstream
//      GoTrue/PostgREST error string (never a secret).
//   4. CONFIRMATION RETRY: after a successful deleteUser the follow-up
//      getUserById can still see the user for a short window (GoTrue
//      read-after-write). The confirmation now retries with a short
//      delay before concluding failure — this removes the most likely
//      source of false "delete_not_confirmed" 500s.
//   5. deleteUser explicitly passes { should_soft_delete:false } and the
//      confirmation also accepts a user carrying deleted_at (soft
//      delete) as confirmed.
//   6. Cascade verification: the caller's profiles row is read before
//      and after deletion (service role bypasses RLS) and the result is
//      logged — proving whether the auth.users FK cascade fired.
// ============================================================================

import { createClient } from "jsr:@supabase/supabase-js@2";

const CORS_HEADERS = {
    "Access-Control-Allow-Origin": "*",
    "Access-Control-Allow-Headers":
        "authorization, x-client-info, apikey, content-type",
    "Access-Control-Allow-Methods": "POST, OPTIONS",
};

/** Confirmation retry tuning (bounded — total ≤ ~1.5 s of waiting). */
const CONFIRM_ATTEMPTS = 3;
const CONFIRM_DELAY_MS = 700;

function logStep(step) {
    console.log(`DELETE_ACCOUNT: ${step}`);
}

/** Extract only safe fields from an upstream error. Never a secret. */
function describeError(err) {
    if (!err) return "unknown error";
    const e = err ?? {};
    const name = e.name ? String(e.name) : "Error";
    const message = e.message ? String(e.message) : String(err);
    const code = e.code ?? e.status ?? e.statusCode ?? null;
    return code != null ? `${name} (${code}): ${message}` : `${name}: ${message}`;
}

/** Safe structured server log: step + error name/message/code only. */
function logError(step, err) {
    console.error(
        JSON.stringify({
            event: "DELETE_ACCOUNT_ERROR",
            step,
            error: describeError(err),
        }),
    );
}

function json(body, status = 200) {
    return new Response(JSON.stringify(body), {
        status,
        headers: { ...CORS_HEADERS, "Content-Type": "application/json" },
    });
}

/** Safe structured error response — no secrets, no tokens, no headers. */
function fail(status, code, step, message, detail = null) {
    return json(
        { success: false, error: code, step, message, detail },
        status,
    );
}

Deno.serve(async (req) => {
    // 1) OPTIONS with 200 (verified working — unchanged).
    if (req.method === "OPTIONS") {
        return new Response("ok", {
            status: 200,
            headers: {
                ...CORS_HEADERS,
                "Access-Control-Allow-Headers":
                    req.headers.get("Access-Control-Request-Headers") ??
                    CORS_HEADERS["Access-Control-Allow-Headers"],
            },
        });
    }
    // 2) POST only.
    if (req.method !== "POST") {
        return fail(405, "method_not_allowed", "method_check", "Use POST.");
    }

    logStep("request_received");

    // Environment — availability is logged as a boolean, never a value.
    const serviceKey = Deno.env.get("SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY") ?? "";
    const supabaseUrl = Deno.env.get("SUPABASE_URL") ?? "";
    if (!serviceKey || !supabaseUrl) {
        logError("env_check", "SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY or SUPABASE_URL not set");
        return fail(
            500,
            "server_misconfigured",
            "env_check",
            "Service is not configured. (Edge Functions → Secrets)",
        );
    }

    // Admin (service-role) client — the current documented Edge pattern.
    const admin = createClient(supabaseUrl, serviceKey, {
        auth: { autoRefreshToken: false, persistSession: false },
        global: { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${serviceKey}` } },
    });
    logStep("admin_client_created");

    // 3) Verify the authenticated caller from the bearer JWT ONLY.
    const authHeader = req.headers.get("Authorization") ?? "";
    if (!authHeader.toLowerCase().startsWith("bearer ")) {
        return fail(401, "no_credentials", "auth_header", "Missing bearer token.");
    }
    logStep("auth_token_found");
    const token = authHeader.slice(7).trim();
    let callerId = "";
    try {
        const { data, error } = await admin.auth.getUser(token);
        if (error || !data?.user?.id) {
            logError("jwt_verify", error ?? "no user in token");
            return fail(401, "invalid_token", "jwt_verify", "Invalid or expired session.");
        }
        callerId = data.user.id;
    } catch (err) {
        logError("jwt_verify", err);
        return fail(401, "invalid_token", "jwt_verify", "Invalid or expired session.");
    }
    logStep("user_verified");

    try {
        // Pre-delete state read (RLS bypassed via service role): proves
        // which migrations are applied and what the cascade must remove.
        // Non-fatal — absence of the tables is a valid degraded state.
        try {
            const { data: p, error: pe } = await admin
                .from("profiles")
                .select("id")
                .eq("id", callerId)
                .maybeSingle();
            const { data: f, error: fe } = await admin
                .from("farms")
                .select("id")
                .eq("user_id", callerId)
                .maybeSingle();
            console.log(
                JSON.stringify({
                    event: "DELETE_ACCOUNT_PRECHECK",
                    user_id: callerId,
                    profiles_row: pe ? `unavailable: ${pe.message}` : p ? "present" : "absent",
                    farms_row: fe ? `unavailable: ${fe.message}` : f ? "present" : "absent",
                }),
            );
        } catch (err) {
            logError("precheck", err);
        }

        // 5) Delete ALL objects belonging ONLY to this user's folder.
        logStep("avatar_cleanup_started");
        let avatarsDeleted = 0;
        try {
            const objects: string[] = [];
            let offset = 0;
            for (;;) {
                const { data, error } = await admin.storage
                    .from("avatars")
                    .list(callerId, {
                        limit: 100,
                        offset,
                        sortBy: { column: "created_at", order: "desc" },
                    });
                if (error) {
                    logError("avatar_list", error);
                    break;
                }
                for (const o of data ?? []) {
                    if (o?.name) objects.push(`${callerId}/${o.name}`);
                }
                if (!data || data.length < 100) break;
                offset += 100;
            }
            if (objects.length) {
                const { error } = await admin.storage
                    .from("avatars")
                    .remove(objects);
                if (error) logError("avatar_remove", error);
                else avatarsDeleted = objects.length;
            }
        } catch (err) {
            // Storage hiccup must not block the account deletion itself;
            // orphaned objects are unreachable once the auth user is gone.
            logError("avatar_cleanup", err);
        }
        logStep("avatar_cleanup_completed");

        // 7) Delete the Auth user (explicit permanent delete). FK CASCADE
        //    (auth.users.id → profiles/farms/land_parcels) removes all
        //    user-owned rows; auth-schema cascades remove sessions.
        logStep("auth_delete_started");
        const { error: delErr } = await admin.auth.deleteUser(callerId, {
            should_soft_delete: false,
        });
        if (delErr) {
            // e.g. FK violations, GoTrue rejections — message is the real
            // upstream error string (no secrets in it).
            logError("auth_delete", delErr);
            return fail(
                500,
                "delete_failed",
                "auth_delete",
                "The account could not be deleted. Nothing has been removed — please try again.",
                describeError(delErr),
            );
        }
        logStep("auth_delete_completed");

        // 8) Verify the auth user no longer exists — with retry, because
        //    a read immediately after delete can still see the user
        //    (GoTrue read-after-write lag). A user carrying deleted_at
        //    counts as confirmed (soft-delete accepted).
        logStep("delete_confirmation_started");
        let confirmed = false;
        let confirmMode = "unknown";
        for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= CONFIRM_ATTEMPTS && !confirmed; attempt++) {
            if (attempt > 1) {
                await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, CONFIRM_DELAY_MS));
            }
            try {
                const { data: check, error: checkErr } = await admin.auth.getUserById(callerId);
                if (checkErr) {
                    confirmed = true; // lookup error ⇒ the user is gone
                    confirmMode = `user_gone_attempt_${attempt}`;
                    break;
                }
                const u: Record<string, unknown> | undefined = check?.user as
                    | Record<string, unknown>
                    | undefined;
                const softDeletedAt =
                    (u?.deleted_at as string | undefined) ??
                    (u?.soft_deleted_at as string | undefined) ??
                    (u?.softDeleteAt as string | undefined) ??
                    null;
                if (softDeletedAt) {
                    confirmed = true;
                    confirmMode = `soft_deleted_at=${softDeletedAt}`;
                } else {
                    confirmMode = `user_still_intact_attempt_${attempt}`;
                }
            } catch (err) {
                logError("delete_confirm", err);
                confirmMode = "confirm_lookup_threw";
            }
        }
        if (!confirmed) {
            return fail(
                500,
                "delete_not_confirmed",
                "delete_confirm",
                "Deletion could not be confirmed. If you were logged out, the account is already gone; otherwise please try again.",
                confirmMode,
            );
        }
        logStep("delete_confirmation_completed");

        // Cascade verification (read-only, non-fatal): the profiles row
        // must be gone after the auth user was deleted — or the table
        // doesn't exist yet (migration not applied).
        let cascade = "unknown";
        try {
            const { data: p2, error: pe2 } = await admin
                .from("profiles")
                .select("id")
                .eq("id", callerId)
                .maybeSingle();
            if (pe2) cascade = `unavailable: ${pe2.message}`;
            else cascade = p2 ? "ROW_STILL_PRESENT (cascade failed!)" : "row_removed";
        } catch (err) {
            logError("cascade_check", err);
        }

        // 9) Success — minimal audit trail, no PII beyond the caller id.
        console.log(
            JSON.stringify({
                event: "account_deleted",
                user_id: callerId,
                avatars_deleted: avatarsDeleted,
                confirm_mode: confirmMode,
                cascade_check: cascade,
                at: new Date().toISOString(),
            }),
        );
        return json({
            success: true,
            data: { userId: callerId, avatarsDeleted, cascade },
        });
    } catch (err) {
        logError("unexpected", err);
        return fail(
            500,
            "unexpected",
            "unexpected",
            "Something went wrong while deleting the account. Please try again.",
            err?.message ? String(err.message) : null,
        );
    }
});

Add a new profile picture editing step to the existing Krisiveda profile avatar upload flow.

Current behavior:
When a user selects a profile picture, it is uploaded directly after compression.

I want to change this flow so the user gets a simple image editor first, similar to the basic profile-picture editing experience in WhatsApp.

NEW FLOW:

Select Photo
→ Basic Profile Picture Editor
→ Confirm / Use Photo
→ Compress
→ Upload to Supabase Storage

Requirements:

1. When the user selects/takes a profile picture, DO NOT upload it immediately.
2. First open a clean, mobile-friendly profile picture editor.
3. The editor should show a large circular preview representing exactly how the profile picture will appear inside the Krisiveda profile icon.
4. The user should be able to reposition the image inside the circular crop area.
5. Allow basic zoom in/out.
6. Allow dragging/panning the image.
7. Keep the circular crop area clearly visible.
8. The area outside the circular crop should be visually dimmed/covered so the user can understand what will actually be visible.
9. The editor should provide a live preview while the user moves or zooms the image.
10. The final uploaded image should be cropped according to the circular profile preview.

UI:

Top:
"Edit Profile Photo"

Center:
Large circular crop/preview area

Controls:
- Zoom out
- Zoom slider or simple zoom control
- Zoom in

Bottom:
"Cancel"        "Use Photo"

Behavior:
- Cancel → discard the selected image and return to the profile popup without uploading anything.
- Use Photo → generate the final cropped image, then run the existing compression process and upload it.
- Do not upload anything before the user presses "Use Photo".

IMPORTANT IMAGE QUALITY:

Keep the improved compression behavior from the existing avatar system.

- Do NOT aggressively compress the final cropped image.
- Use high-quality JPEG/WebP compression around 85–90%.
- Keep the final cropped image sufficiently high resolution for a sharp profile picture.
- Do not repeatedly compress the same image.
- Crop first, then compress once, then upload.
- Avoid unnecessary downscaling.
- Keep the existing 20 MB original-file validation.

SUPABASE STORAGE:

Keep the existing secure avatar system unchanged.

Continue using:
`avatars/<user_id>/...`

The avatar must remain associated only with the currently authenticated user's ID.

Do not change:
- Supabase authentication
- Storage bucket
- Storage security policies
- Avatar ownership logic
- Profile database structure
- Existing logout/login avatar isolation
- Existing profile popup design

DESIGN:

Make the editor visually consistent with the existing Krisiveda UI:
- Dark/glass appearance
- Subtle blur
- Rounded corners
- Clean modern layout
- Mobile-first
- Responsive on desktop and mobile

Do NOT make it overly complicated like a full photo editor.

This is only a basic profile-picture editor similar to WhatsApp:
- Circular crop
- Move image
- Zoom image
- Preview
- Confirm

IMPORTANT:
Reuse the existing avatar upload/compression code wherever possible instead of creating a second upload system.

The final flow must be:

User clicks camera/profile photo
→ selects photo
→ editor opens
→ user adjusts crop/zoom
→ clicks "Use Photo"
→ crop is generated
→ high-quality compression happens once
→ upload to Supabase
→ profile avatar updates

Do not upload the original selected image directly.
Do not change any unrelated profile UI or functionality.

/* ---------------- display name (server truth) ----------------
   The name is persisted in TWO places (spec: cross-device + survives
   login): the `profiles` row (data layer) and the auth user's
   user_metadata (so toAuthUser() shows it on every future session
   without an extra fetch). Degrades softly like the avatar flow. */
export async function updateProfileName(userId, name) {
    if (!userId || !supabase) return false;
    const trimmed = String(name || '').trim();
    if (!trimmed) return false;
    try {
        const { error } = await supabase
            .from("profiles")
            .upsert(
                { id: userId, full_name: trimmed, updated_at: new Date().toISOString() },
                { onConflict: "id" },
            );
        if (error) {
            if (!isSchemaError(error)) {
                warn("profile name save failed", error);
                return false;
            }
            warn("profile name save — migration not applied", error);
            return "degraded";
        }
        return true;
    } catch (err) {
        warn("profile name save threw", err);
        return false;
    }
}

/** Mirror the name into auth user_metadata (read on EVERY session by
 *  toAuthUser → useAuth). Best-effort: a failure here doesn't fail the
 *  save — the profiles row already carries the new name. */
export async function updateUserMetadataName(name) {
    if (!supabase) return false;
    try {
        const { error } = await supabase.auth.updateUser({
            data: { full_name: name },
        });
        if (error) {
            warn("user_metadata name update failed", error);
            return false;
        }
        return true;
    } catch (err) {
        warn("user_metadata name update threw", err);
        return false;
    }
}

/** Persist the user's display name: profiles.name (data truth) +
 *  auth user_metadata.full_name (session truth). Returns
 *  { ok } on success, { ok:false, degraded } when the server layer is
 *  absent (metadata sync still applied), { ok:false } on real failure.
 *  Never throws — callers render their own error state. */
export async function saveDisplayName(userId, name) {
  const trimmed = String(name || "").trim();
  if (!userId || !supabase || !trimmed) return { ok: false };

  // 1) Session truth first: user_metadata.full_name is what toAuthUser
  //    reads on every future session (refresh / next login). The auth
  //    layer is already live, so this alone fixes persistence.
  try {
    const { error } = await supabase.auth.updateUser({
      data: { full_name: trimmed },
    });
    if (error) {
      if (!isSchemaError(error)) {
        warn("name update failed", error);
        return { ok: false };
      }
      warn("name update — degraded auth layer", error);
      return { ok: false, degraded: true };
    }
  } catch (err) {
    warn("name update threw", err);
    return { ok: false };
  }

  // 2) Data truth: the profiles row (same table/columns the avatar flow
  //    uses; upsert onConflict id — no new record is invented, the row
  //    for THIS authenticated user id is written or updated).
  try {
    const { error } = await supabase
      .from("profiles")
      .upsert(
        { id: userId, name: trimmed, updated_at: new Date().toISOString() },
        { onConflict: "id" },
      );
    if (error) {
      if (isSchemaError(error)) {
        warn("profiles.name save — migration not applied", error);
        return { ok: true, degraded: true }; // metadata write already succeeded
      }
      warn("profiles.name save failed", error);
      return { ok: false, degraded: true }; // metadata write already succeeded
    }
  } catch (err) {
    warn("profiles.name save threw", err);
  }
  return { ok: true };
}

**The fix (3 files, no new tables/columns, avatar flow untouched):**

- **[profileService.js](src/lib/profileService.js#L405-L467)** — new `saveDisplayName(userId, name)`: writes `profiles.name` (existing table, upsert on `id` for the authenticated user — never a second record) **and** `auth.user_metadata.full_name` (the field `toAuthUser` reads on every future session). Degrades gracefully exactly like the avatar pipeline: while the avatar/profiles migration is still unapplied in your environment, the profiles-row write fails softly but the auth-metadata write still persists the name.
- **[useAuth.jsx](src/hooks/useAuth.jsx)** — new `updateUserName()`: patches the single session source of truth so every consumer (popup, dashboard greeting, initials) re-renders immediately with the new name — no reload, no second state system, and the stale-metadata overwrite is impossible by construction.
- **[Header.jsx](src/components/layout/Header.jsx)** — `saveProfile` is now async with a `savingProfile` busy flag (Save disabled, "…" state, `aria-busy`, double-submit guard). It only hits the server when the name actually changed (role-only saves never blocked), writes server → optimistic local cache → session patch, then closes the edit pane. - **[translations.js](src/data/translations.js)** — `common.profile.nameSaveFailed` (en + bn).

- Edit field pre-fills with current effective name ✓
- Save → edit pane closes → popup shows **"Ananta"** immediately, no reload ✓
- Page reload → still **"Ananta"** (from persisted session metadata, as the real `updateUser` write would leave it), dashboard greeting shows it too ✓
- Failure path: editor stays open + clear error, no fake success ✓
- Build ✓, lint **18w/0e** (baseline), 8 test keys purged — 0 remaining

One honest caveat: `profiles.name` row-write couldn't be end-to-end confirmed with a forged token against the real backend (it degrades softly, as designed). Language dropdown fixed — root causes addressed, not just z-index.

**Diagnosis (live):** the menu was absolutely positioned inside the profile popup's `overflow: auto` scroll wrapper (a clipping context), rendered **upward over the 422px hero photo** with a translucent `rgba(12,18,15,0.92)` background — so the photo bled through behind the text — and its `translateX(-50%)` centering pushed it past the popup's left edge (measured `left: −0.1px`).

**The fix** — the menu now renders through `createPortal` under `<body>` as `position: fixed`:
- **Never clipped**: it's no longer a descendant of the scroll container, so no ancestor overflow can cut it off
- **Anchored to the button**: measured from the Language button's live rect — left-aligned with it, clamped to stay inside the viewport; opens **8px below the button**, auto-flipping above (bottom-anchored, same 8px gap) only when there's genuinely no room below
- **Tracks the button**: position lives in React state and recomputes on window resize and any scroll (capture phase) — verified the menu follows the button through both
- **Solid background**: dark `#101712` / light `#fffdf9` — opaque, so the photo can't interfere with text in either theme; `z-index: 90`
- **Behavior untouched**: same `prefMenu` state, same `changeLanguage` on click, active language still highlighted, outside-click still closes it (the handler now also tolerates clicks inside the portaled menu)

**Files**: [Header.jsx](src/components/layout/Header.jsx) (portal render + measured anchor + tracking effect + `langMenuRef` in the outside-click guard), [Header.css](src/components/layout/Header.css) (fixed/solid menu rules).

**Live-verified**: desktop 1280×800 — opens below with exact 8px gap, left-aligned, fully in viewport, all 5 options (English, বাংলা, हिन्दी, తెలుగు, தமிழ்) rendered; বাংলা click switched the whole app immediately and closed the menu; outside-click closes; active option tracked in both languages; light mode contrast confirmed (dark ink on warm white, accent options); mobile 375px — clamped, left-aligned, flipped above correctly, fully visible; no horizontal overflow anywhere.
